## API Reference

### `@effect/ai-amazon-bedrock/AmazonBedrockClient`

#### `AmazonBedrockClient.AmazonBedrockClient`

**Replacement:** `none`

The @effect/ai-amazon-bedrock provider package was removed from v4, so AmazonBedrockClient has no direct replacement. Use @aws-sdk/client-bedrock-runtime directly or build a custom v4 provider integration.

### `@effect/ai/AiError`

#### `AiError.AiError`

**Replacement:** `AiError.AiError`

Moved to effect/unstable/ai/AiError and redesigned from a union of separately tagged errors into one AiError wrapper with a semantic reason. Construct it with AiError.make({ module, method, reason }) and match error.reason rather than the old top-level tags.

**Before**

```ts
export type AiError = HttpRequestError | HttpResponseError | MalformedInput | MalformedOutput | UnknownError;
```

#### `AiError.HttpRequestError`

**Replacement:** `AiError.make + AiError.NetworkError`

Replace the old top-level request error with an AiError whose reason is NetworkError. NetworkError.fromRequestError converts a v4 HttpClientError.RequestError.

**Before**

```ts
export declare class HttpRequestError extends HttpRequestError_base { readonly [TypeId]: TypeId; static fromRequestError({ error, ...params }: { readonly module: string; readonly method: string; readonly error: HttpClientError.RequestError; }): HttpRequestError; get message(): string; }
```

#### `AiError.HttpResponseError`

**Replacement:** `AiError.make + AiError.reasonFromHttpStatus / AiError.InvalidOutputError`

There is no single v4 response-error class. Wrap a semantic reason with AiError.make: use reasonFromHttpStatus for status failures and InvalidOutputError for decode or empty-body failures.

**Before**

```ts
export declare class HttpResponseError extends HttpResponseError_base { readonly [TypeId]: TypeId; static fromResponseError({ error, ...params }: { readonly module: string; readonly method: string; readonly error: HttpClientError.ResponseError; }): Effect.Effect<never, HttpResponseError>; get message(): string; }
```

#### `AiError.MalformedInput`

**Replacement:** `AiError.make + AiError.InvalidUserInputError`

Replace the old top-level input error with an AiError whose reason is InvalidUserInputError. Use InvalidRequestError when the provider request parameters themselves are malformed.

**Before**

```ts
export declare class MalformedInput extends MalformedInput_base { readonly [TypeId]: TypeId; }
```

#### `AiError.MalformedOutput`

**Replacement:** `AiError.make + AiError.InvalidOutputError`

Replace the old top-level output error with an AiError whose reason is InvalidOutputError. The old fromParseError helper becomes InvalidOutputError.fromSchemaError.

**Before**

```ts
export declare class MalformedOutput extends MalformedOutput_base { readonly [TypeId]: TypeId; static fromParseError({ error, ...params }: { readonly module: string; readonly method: string; readonly description?: string; readonly error: ParseError; }): MalformedOutput; }
```

#### `AiError.TypeId`

**Replacement:** `AiError.isAiError`

The AiError brand is private in v4. Use isAiError for runtime narrowing, or isAiErrorReason for a reason, instead of inspecting or constructing the type id.

**Before**

```ts
export type TypeId = typeof TypeId;
```

#### `AiError.UnknownError`

**Replacement:** `AiError.make + AiError.UnknownError`

UnknownError is now a semantic reason rather than a top-level error. Put module and method on AiError.make and inspect reason._tag when handling the outer AiError.

**Before**

```ts
export declare class UnknownError extends UnknownError_base { readonly [TypeId]: TypeId; get message(): string; }
```

**Replacement:** `Prompt.concat`

Renamed in v4. concat preserves the old dual API and concatenates the messages from a Prompt with additional raw input.

### `@effect/ai/Tool`

#### `Tool.AnyParametersSchema`

**Replacement:** `Schema.Constraint`

The AI-specific alias was removed. V4 Tool parameter schemas use the general Schema.Constraint type and are no longer restricted to the old struct-or-EmptyParams union.

**Before**

```ts
export type AnyParametersSchema = AnyStructSchema | EmptyParams;
```

#### `Tool.AnyTaggedRequestSchema`

**Replacement:** `none`

The TaggedRequest-specific Tool adapter contract was removed. Model the operation directly with Tool.make and ordinary v4 Schema.Constraint values.

**Before**

```ts

```

#### `Tool.Destructive`

**Replacement:** `Tool.Destructive`

Moved to effect/unstable/ai/Tool. It is now a Context.Reference<boolean> value rather than a Reference subclass; its default remains true.

**Before**

```ts
export declare class Destructive extends Destructive_base { }
```

#### `Tool.Failure`

**Replacement:** `Tool.Failure`

Moved to effect/unstable/ai/Tool and remains the utility type that extracts a tool's decoded failure type.

**Before**

```ts
export type Failure<T> = T extends Tool<infer _Name, infer _Config, infer _Requirements> ? Schema.Schema.Type<_Config["failure"]> : never;
```

#### `Tool.FromTaggedRequest`

**Replacement:** `Tool.Tool`

The dedicated derived alias was removed. Construct with Tool.make and let Tool.Tool infer the name, parameter, success, and failure schemas.

**Before**

```ts

```

#### `Tool.Idempotent`

**Replacement:** `Tool.Idempotent`

Moved to effect/unstable/ai/Tool. It is now a Context.Reference<boolean> value rather than a Reference subclass; its default remains false.

**Before**

```ts
export declare class Idempotent extends Idempotent_base { }
```

#### `Tool.OpenWorld`

**Replacement:** `Tool.OpenWorld`

Moved to effect/unstable/ai/Tool. It is now a Context.Reference<boolean> value rather than a Reference subclass; its default remains true.

**Before**

```ts
export declare class OpenWorld extends OpenWorld_base { }
```

#### `Tool.ProviderDefinedTypeId`

**Replacement:** `Tool.ProviderDefinedTypeId`

Moved to effect/unstable/ai/Tool and remains public. Its literal changed, so use the export rather than retaining the old hard-coded string.

**Before**

```ts
export type ProviderDefinedTypeId = typeof ProviderDefinedTypeId;
```

#### `Tool.Readonly`

**Replacement:** `Tool.Readonly`

Moved to effect/unstable/ai/Tool. It is now a Context.Reference<boolean> value rather than a Reference subclass; its default remains false.

**Before**

```ts
export declare class Readonly extends Readonly_base { }
```

#### `Tool.Requirements`

**Replacement:** `Tool.HandlerServices`

Renamed and refined. HandlerServices combines parameter-decoding, result-encoding, and request-level dependencies required by a tool handler.

**Before**

```ts
export type Requirements<T> = T extends Tool<infer _Name, infer _Config, infer _Requirements> ? _Config["parameters"]["Context"] | _Config["success"]["Context"] | _Config["failure"]["Context"] | _Requirements : never;
```

#### `Tool.Success`

**Replacement:** `Tool.Success`

Moved to effect/unstable/ai/Tool and remains the utility type that extracts a tool's decoded success type.

**Before**

```ts
export type Success<T> = T extends Tool<infer _Name, infer _Config, infer _Requirements> ? Schema.Schema.Type<_Config["success"]> : never;
```

#### `Tool.Title`

**Replacement:** `Tool.Title`

Moved to effect/unstable/ai/Tool. It is now a Context.Service annotation key; continue attaching the string title with tool.annotate(Tool.Title, value).

**Before**

```ts
export declare class Title extends Title_base { }
```

#### `Tool.Tool.ProviderDefinedProto`

**Replacement:** `Tool.ProviderDefined`

This implementation-brand interface is no longer public. Use Tool.ProviderDefined for the model type and Tool.isProviderDefined for runtime narrowing.

**Before**

```ts

```

#### `Tool.Tool.Variance`

**Replacement:** `Tool.Tool / Tool.Any`

This implementation variance interface is no longer public; its requirement marker is inline in Tool.Tool. Constrain generic code with Tool.Tool or Tool.Any.

**Before**

```ts

```

#### `Tool.Tool.VarianceStruct`

**Replacement:** `Tool.Tool / Tool.Any`

This implementation variance payload is no longer public; the requirements marker is inline in Tool.Tool and should not be named independently.

**Before**

```ts
interface VarianceStruct<out Requirements> { readonly _Requirements: Covariant<Requirements>; }
```

#### `Tool.TypeId`

**Replacement:** `Tool.TypeId`

Moved to effect/unstable/ai/Tool and remains public. Its literal changed, so use the export rather than retaining the old hard-coded string.

**Before**

```ts
export type TypeId = typeof TypeId;
```

#### `Tool.fromTaggedRequest`

**Replacement:** `Tool.make`

The adapter was removed. Rebuild the tool explicitly with Tool.make(name, { parameters, success, failure }); Toolkit.make no longer converts schema values automatically.

#### `Tool.getDescriptionFromSchemaAst`

**Replacement:** `SchemaAST.resolveDescription`

Moved out of Tool to the general v4 AST annotation resolver. For a Tool value, prefer Tool.getDescription.

#### `Tool.getJsonSchemaFromSchemaAst`

**Replacement:** `Tool.getJsonSchemaFromSchema`

Renamed to accept a Schema.Constraint instead of a raw AST and now emits the v4 JSON Schema model. Wrap a raw AST with Schema.make first.

**Before**

```ts

```

**Replacement:** `Toolkit.make`

#### `Args.All.ArgsAny`

**Replacement:** `Command.Command.Config.Infer`

Infer the output of a command config record; standalone argument collections were removed.

**Replacement:** `Argument.Argument`

export declare namespace Args { interface Variance<A> { readonly [ArgsTypeId]: { readonly _A: (_: never) => A; }; } interface BaseArgsConfig { readonly name?: string; } interface PathArgsConfig extends BaseArgsConfig { readonly exists?: Primitive.PathExists; } interface FormatArgsConfig extends BaseArgsConfig { readonly format?: "json" | "yaml" | "ini" | "toml"; } }

**Replacement:** `Primitive.FileParseOptions`

Pass the name separately and use the format option with Argument.fileParse or Argument.fileSchema.

**Replacement:** `Argument.path(name, { pathType, mustExist })`

**Replacement:** `Argument.Argument`

#### `Args.ArgsTypeId`

**Replacement:** `Param.isParam(value) && value.kind === Param.argumentKind`

**Replacement:** `Command.make(name, config)`

Collect arguments in the config record passed to Command.make; there is no standalone Argument.all.

**Replacement:** `Argument.atLeast`

#### `Args.atMost`

**Replacement:** `Argument.atMost`

Use the moved combinator.

**Before**

### `@effect/cli/Options`

#### `Options.All.OptionsAny`

**Replacement:** `Param.AnyFlag`

Use the shared any-flag-parameter type.

**Before**

```ts

```

#### `Options.All.Return`

**Replacement:** `Command.Command.Config.Infer`

Infer the output of a command config record; standalone flag collections were removed.

**Before**

```ts

```

#### `Options.Options`

**Replacement:** `Flag.Flag`

Options was renamed to Flag in effect/unstable/cli.

**Before**

```ts
export interface Options<A> extends Options.Variance<A>, Pipeable { }
export declare namespace Options { interface Variance<A> { readonly [OptionsTypeId]: { _A: (_: never) => A; }; } interface BooleanOptionsConfig { readonly ifPresent?: boolean; readonly negationNames?: ReadonlyArray<string>; readonly aliases?: ReadonlyArray<string>; } interface PathOptionsConfig { readonly exists?: Primitive.PathExists; } }
```

#### `Options.Options.BooleanOptionsConfig`

**Replacement:** `Flag.boolean + Flag.withAlias + Flag.map`

The config object was removed; aliases and value inversion are combinators, while custom negation names need application logic.

**Before**

```ts
interface BooleanOptionsConfig { readonly ifPresent?: boolean; readonly negationNames?: ReadonlyArray<string>; readonly aliases?: ReadonlyArray<string>; }
```

#### `Options.Options.PathOptionsConfig`

**Replacement:** `{ readonly mustExist?: boolean }`

Path options are inline; true replaces exists=yes and omission replaces either. exists=no has no exact replacement.

**Before**

```ts
interface PathOptionsConfig { readonly exists?: Primitive.PathExists; }
```

#### `Options.Options.Variance`

**Replacement:** `Flag.Flag`

The separate variance artifact was removed; Flag inherits the shared Param variance.

**Before**

```ts
interface Variance<A> { readonly [OptionsTypeId]: { _A: (_: never) => A; }; }
```

#### `Options.OptionsTypeId`

**Replacement:** `Param.isParam(value) && value.kind === Param.flagKind`

The public Options type id was removed; use the Param guard and flag kind discriminator.

**Before**

```ts

```

#### `Options.all`

**Replacement:** `Command.make(name, config)`

Collect flags in the config record passed to Command.make; there is no standalone Flag.all.

**Before**

```ts
all: <const Arg extends Iterable<Options<any>> | Record<string, Options<any>>>(arg: Arg) => All.Return<Arg>
```

#### `Options.atLeast`

**Replacement:** `Flag.atLeast`

Use the moved combinator; v4 returns ReadonlyArray rather than NonEmptyArray.

**Before**

```ts

```

#### `Options.atMost`

**Replacement:** `Flag.atMost`

Use the moved combinator.

**Before**

```ts

#### `Options.between`

**Replacement:** `Flag.between`

Use the moved combinator; v4 validates bounds when constructing the parameter.

**Before**

```ts
between: { (min: 0, max: number): <A>(self: Options<A>) => Options<Array<A>>; (min: number, max: number): <A>(self: Options<A>) => Options<NonEmptyArray<A>>; <A>(self: Options<A>, min: 0, max: number): Options<Array<A>>; <A>(self: Options<A>, min: number, max: number): Options<NonEmptyArray<A>>; }
```

#### `Options.boolean`

**Replacement:** `Flag.boolean`

Use the moved constructor; --no-name is automatic and aliases are added with Flag.withAlias.

#### `Options.choice`

**Replacement:** `Flag.choice`

**Replacement:** `Flag.file`

Use mustExist=true for exists=yes and omit it for either; exists=no has no exact replacement.

**Replacement:** `Flag.float`

Use the moved constructor.

**Replacement:** `none`

#### `Options.getIdentifier`

**Replacement:** `none`

#### `Options.getUsage`

**Replacement:** `none`

The public Usage tree was removed; Command generates a usage string internally.

#### `Options.integer`

**Replacement:** `Flag.integer`

Use the moved constructor.

**Before**

#### `Options.isBool`

**Replacement:** `none`

No public flag-shape predicate remains; boolean-shape inspection is internal.

#### `Options.isOptions`

**Replacement:** `Param.isParam(value) && value.kind === Param.flagKind`

**Replacement:** `Flag.keyValuePair`

Renamed and now returns Record<string, string> rather than HashMap.

#### `Options.map`

**Replacement:** `Flag.map`

Use the moved combinator.

**Before**

```ts

#### `Options.mapEffect`

**Replacement:** `Flag.mapEffect`

Use the moved combinator; mapping failures are CliError.

**Before**

```ts

**Replacement:** `Flag.mapTryCatch`

Use the moved combinator; onError now returns a string rather than HelpDoc.

**Before**

```

V4 Flag.none is an always-failing sentinel, not v3's empty successful option set.

#### `Options.optional`

**Replacement:** `Flag.optional`

**Replacement:** `Flag.orElse(() => fallback)`

**Replacement:** `none`

#### `Primitive.getHelp`

**Replacement:** `none`

**Replacement:** `Primitive.integer`

**Replacement:** `none`

The boolean Primitive predicate is internal in v4.

} interface Handlers<State, Output> { readonly render: (state: State, action: Action<State, Output>) => Effect<string, never, Environment>; readonly process: (input: UserInput, state: State) => Effect<Action<State, Output>, never, Environment>; readonly deny: string; }; readonly placeholder?: { readonly defaultConfirm?: string; readonly defaultDeny?: string; }; } interface DateOptions { readonly message: string; readonly initial?: globalThis.Date; readonly dateMask?: string; readonly validate?: (value: globalThis.Date) => Effect<globalThis.Date, string>; readonly locales?: { readonly months: [ string, string, string, string, string, string, string, string, string, string, string, string ]; readonly monthsShort: [ string, string, string, string, string, string, string, string, string, string, string, string ]; readonly weekdays: [string, string, string, string, string, string, string]; readonly weekdaysShort: [string, string, string, string, string, string, string]; }; } interface IntegerOptions { readonly message: string; readonly min?: number; readonly max?: number; readonly incrementBy?: number; readonly decrementBy?: number; readonly validate?: (value: number) => Effect<number, string>; } interface FloatOptions extends IntegerOptions { readonly precision?: number; } interface ListOptions extends TextOptions { readonly delimiter?: string; } interface FileOptions { readonly type?: Primitive.PathType; readonly message?: string; readonly startingPath?: string; readonly maxPerPage?: number; readonly filter?: (file: string) => boolean | Effect<boolean, never, Environment>; } interface SelectOptions<A> { readonly message: string; readonly choices: ReadonlyArray<SelectChoice<A>>; readonly maxPerPage?: number; } interface MultiSelectOptions { readonly selectAll?: string; readonly selectNone?: string; readonly inverseSelection?: string; readonly min?: number; readonly max?: number; } interface SelectChoice<A> { readonly title: string; readonly value: A; readonly description?: string; readonly disabled?: boolean; readonly selected?: boolean; } interface TextOptions { readonly message: string; readonly default?: string; readonly validate?: (value: string) => Effect<string, string>; } interface ToggleOptions { readonly message: string; readonly initial?: boolean; readonly active?: string; readonly inactive?: string; } }

```

**After**

```ts
export type ServeOptions<R extends string> = (Bun.Serve.UnixServeOptions<WebSocketContext> | Bun.Serve.HostnamePortServeOptions<WebSocketContext>) & { readonly routes?: Bun.Serve.Routes<WebSocketContext, R>; };
```

- `BunHttpServer.layerContext` -> `BunHttpServer.layerHttpServices`: Direct rename; it provides HttpPlatform, Etag.Generator, and BunServices.

### `@effect/platform-bun/BunHttpServerRequest`

- `BunHttpServerRequest.toRequest` -> `BunHttpServerRequest.toBunServerRequest`: Direct rename with the more precise Bun.BunRequest result type.

### `@effect/platform-bun/BunSink`

- `BunSink.stderr` -> `stdio.stderr() from Stdio.Stdio`: Process stdio moved behind effect/Stdio; provide BunStdio.layer. stderr remains a Sink and can be configured with endOnDone.

- `BunSink.stdin` -> `stdio.stdin from Stdio.Stdio`: Standard input is correctly modeled as a Stream in v4, not a writable Sink; manually adapt process.stdin only if writing to it was intentional.

- `BunSink.stdout` -> `stdio.stdout() from Stdio.Stdio`: Process stdio moved behind effect/Stdio; provide BunStdio.layer. stdout remains a Sink.

### `@effect/platform-bun/BunSocket`

#### `BunSocket.NetSocket`

**Replacement:** `BunSocket.NetSocket`

The identifier remains, but the old interface/tag pair is now one Context.Service for node:net.Socket.

**Before**

```ts
export interface NetSocket { readonly _: unique symbol }
```

**After**

```ts
export class NetSocket extends Context.Service<NetSocket, Net.Socket>()( "@effect/platform-node/NodeSocket/NetSocket" ) {}
```

### `@effect/platform-bun/BunSocketServer`

#### `BunSocketServer.IncomingMessage`

**Replacement:** `BunSocketServer.IncomingMessage`

The identifier remains and is now a Context.Service for node:http.IncomingMessage.

**Before**

```ts

```

**After**

```ts

```

### `@effect/platform-bun/BunStream`

#### `BunStream.FromReadableOptions`

**Replacement:** `Pick<Parameters<typeof BunStream.fromReadable>[0], "chunkSize" | "closeOnDone">`

The named interface was inlined into the constructor options; chunkSize is now a number and the full options also contain evaluate, onError, and bufferSize.

**Before**

```ts
export interface FromReadableOptions { readonly chunkSize?: SizeInput readonly closeOnDone?: boolean | undefined }
```

#### `BunStream.FromWritableOptions`

**Replacement:** `Pick<Parameters<typeof BunSink.fromWritable>[0], "endOnDone" | "encoding">`

The named interface was inlined into BunSink.fromWritable and duplex constructor options.

**Before**

```ts
export interface FromWritableOptions { readonly endOnDone?: boolean readonly encoding?: BufferEncoding }
```

#### `BunStream.stderr`

**Replacement:** `stdio.stderr() from Stdio.Stdio`

Standard error is correctly modeled as a Sink in v4. Explicitly adapt process.stderr with BunStream.fromReadable only to preserve the old unusual read behavior.

**Before**

```ts
stderr: Stream.Stream<Uint8Array> = internal.fromReadable(() => process.stderr, (err) => err, { closeOnDone: false }).pipe(Stream.orDie)
```

#### `BunStream.stdin`

**Replacement:** `stdio.stdin from Stdio.Stdio`

Standard input moved to the Stdio service; provide BunStdio.layer. Its stream exposes PlatformError instead of dying.

**Before**

```ts
stdin: Stream.Stream<Uint8Array> = internal.fromReadable(() => process.stdin, (err) => err, { closeOnDone: false }).pipe(Stream.orDie)
```

#### `BunStream.stdout`

**Replacement:** `stdio.stdout() from Stdio.Stdio`

Standard output is correctly modeled as a Sink in v4. Explicitly adapt process.stdout with BunStream.fromReadable only to preserve the old unusual read behavior.

**Before**

```ts
stdout: Stream.Stream<Uint8Array> = internal.fromReadable(() => process.stdout, (err) => err, { closeOnDone: false }).pipe(Stream.orDie)
```

WorkerManager was removed. Provide WorkerPlatform directly, or use BunWorker.layer(spawn) when a Worker.Spawner is also required.

```

**Replacement:** `@effect/platform-node/NodeMultipart#stream`

### `@effect/platform-node-shared/NodeSink`

- `NodeSink.stderr` -> `stdio.stderr() from Stdio.Stdio`: Standard error moved to effect/Stdio; provide NodeStdio.layer or NodeServices.layer.

- `NodeSink.stdin` -> `NodeSink.fromWritable({ evaluate: () => process.stdin, onError: ... })`: There is no Stdio sink because stdin is a readable stream in v4; use a manual adapter only if writing to process.stdin was intentional.

- `NodeSink.stdout` -> `stdio.stdout() from Stdio.Stdio`: Standard output moved to effect/Stdio; provide NodeStdio.layer or NodeServices.layer.

### `@effect/platform-node-shared/NodeSocket`

#### `NodeSocket.NetSocket`

**Replacement:** `NodeSocket.NetSocket`

The identifier remains, but the old interface/tag pair is now one Context.Service; use NodeSocket.NetSocket["Service"] for the node:net.Socket value type.

export interface NetSocket { readonly _: unique symbol; }
```

**After**

```

### `@effect/platform-node-shared/NodeStream`

#### `NodeStream.FromReadableOptions`

**Replacement:** `{ readonly chunkSize?: number; readonly closeOnDone?: boolean }`

The named interface was removed and its fields were inlined into readable constructor options; chunkSize narrowed from SizeInput to number.

**Before**

```ts
export interface FromReadableOptions { readonly chunkSize?: SizeInput; readonly closeOnDone?: boolean | undefined; }
```

#### `NodeStream.FromWritableOptions`

**Replacement:** `{ readonly endOnDone?: boolean; readonly encoding?: BufferEncoding }`

The named interface was removed and its fields were inlined into NodeSink and duplex constructor options.

**Before**

```ts
export interface FromWritableOptions { readonly endOnDone?: boolean; readonly encoding?: BufferEncoding; }
```

- `NodeStream.stderr` -> `NodeStream.fromReadable({ evaluate: () => process.stderr, closeOnDone: false }).pipe(Stream.orDie)`: This preserves the unusual v3 read behavior; for normal error output use the stdio.stderr() Sink from effect/Stdio.

- `NodeStream.stdin` -> `stdio.stdin from Stdio.Stdio`: Standard input moved to effect/Stdio; provide NodeStdio.layer or NodeServices.layer. The service stream exposes PlatformError instead of dying.

- `NodeStream.stdout` -> `NodeStream.fromReadable({ evaluate: () => process.stdout, closeOnDone: false }).pipe(Stream.orDie)`: This preserves the unusual v3 read behavior; for normal output use the stdio.stdout() Sink from effect/Stdio.

**Replacement:** `undici.Agent`

**Before**

```ts
declare class Agent extends Dispatcher { constructor (opts?: Agent.Options) closed: boolean destroyed: boolean dispatch (options: Agent.DispatchOptions, handler: Dispatcher.DispatchHandler): boolean readonly stats: Record<string, TClientStats | TPoolStats> }
declare namespace Agent { export interface Options extends Pool.Options { factory?(origin: string | URL, opts: Object): Dispatcher; maxRedirections?: number; interceptors?: { Agent?: readonly Dispatcher.DispatchInterceptor[] } & Pool.Options['interceptors'] } export interface DispatchOptions extends Dispatcher.DispatchOptions { maxRedirections?: number; } }
```

**After**

```ts
declare class Agent extends Dispatcher { constructor (opts?: Agent.Options) closed: boolean destroyed: boolean dispatch (options: Agent.DispatchOptions, handler: Dispatcher.DispatchHandler): boolean readonly stats: Record<string, TClientStats | TPoolStats> }
declare namespace Agent { export interface Options extends Pool.Options { factory?(origin: string | URL, opts: Object): Dispatcher; maxOrigins?: number } export interface DispatchOptions extends Dispatcher.DispatchOptions { } }
```

**Replacement:** `undici.Agent.DispatchOptions`

Import the same Agent namespace type from undici; Undici 8 removes maxRedirections.

**Before**

```

**After**

```ts

```

**Replacement:** `undici.Agent.Options`

Import the same Agent namespace type; Undici 8 removes maxRedirections and option-level interceptors, adds maxOrigins, and uses dispatcher.compose for interceptors.

**Before**

```ts

```

**After**

```ts
export interface Options extends Pool.Options { factory?(origin: string | URL, opts: Object): Dispatcher; maxOrigins?: number }
```

Import the upstream Client directly; custom handlers must use Undici 8's controller-based v2 handler API.

declare class ProxyAgent extends Dispatcher { constructor (options: ProxyAgent.Options | string) dispatch (options: Agent.DispatchOptions, handler: Dispatcher.DispatchHandler): boolean close (): Promise<void> }
declare namespace ProxyAgent { export interface Options extends Agent.Options { uri: string; auth?: string; token?: string; headers?: IncomingHttpHeaders; requestTls?: buildConnector.BuildOptions; proxyTls?: buildConnector.BuildOptions; clientFactory?(origin: URL, opts: object): Dispatcher; proxyTunnel?: boolean; } }
```

**After**

```ts
declare class ProxyAgent extends Dispatcher { constructor (options: ProxyAgent.Options | string) dispatch (options: Agent.DispatchOptions, handler: Dispatcher.DispatchHandler): boolean close (): Promise<void> }
declare namespace ProxyAgent { export interface Options extends Agent.Options { uri: string; auth?: string; token?: string; headers?: OutgoingHttpHeaders; requestTls?: buildConnector.BuildOptions; proxyTls?: buildConnector.BuildOptions; clientFactory?(origin: URL, opts: object): Dispatcher; proxyTunnel?: boolean; } }
```

#### `Undici.ProxyAgent.Options`

**Replacement:** `undici.ProxyAgent.Options`

Import the same ProxyAgent namespace type; Undici 8 types proxy headers as OutgoingHttpHeaders.

**Before**

```ts
export interface Options extends Agent.Options { uri: string; auth?: string; token?: string; headers?: IncomingHttpHeaders; requestTls?: buildConnector.BuildOptions; proxyTls?: buildConnector.BuildOptions; clientFactory?(origin: URL, opts: object): Dispatcher; proxyTunnel?: boolean; }
```

**After**

```ts
export interface Options extends Agent.Options { uri: string; auth?: string; token?: string; headers?: OutgoingHttpHeaders; requestTls?: buildConnector.BuildOptions; proxyTls?: buildConnector.BuildOptions; clientFactory?(origin: URL, opts: object): Dispatcher; proxyTunnel?: boolean; }
```

#### `Undici.RedirectHandler`

**Replacement:** `undici.RedirectHandler`

Import the upstream class; Undici 8 removes redirectionLimitReached from the constructor and adds static buildDispatch.

**Before**

```ts
export declare class RedirectHandler implements Dispatcher.DispatchHandler { constructor ( dispatch: Dispatcher.Dispatch, maxRedirections: number, opts: Dispatcher.DispatchOptions, handler: Dispatcher.DispatchHandler, redirectionLimitReached: boolean ) }
```

**After**

```ts
export declare class RedirectHandler implements Dispatcher.DispatchHandler { static buildDispatch (dispatcher: Dispatcher, maxRedirections: number): Dispatcher.Dispatch constructor ( dispatch: Dispatcher.Dispatch, maxRedirections: number, opts: Dispatcher.DispatchOptions, handler: Dispatcher.DispatchHandler ) }
```

#### `Undici.Request`

**Replacement:** `undici.Request`

Import Undici's named Request directly; clone is a method in Undici 8.

**Before**

```ts
export declare class Request extends BodyMixin { constructor (input: RequestInfo, init?: RequestInit) readonly cache: RequestCache readonly credentials: RequestCredentials readonly destination: RequestDestination readonly headers: Headers readonly integrity: string readonly method: string readonly mode: RequestMode readonly redirect: RequestRedirect readonly referrer: string readonly referrerPolicy: ReferrerPolicy readonly url: string readonly keepalive: boolean readonly signal: AbortSignal readonly duplex: RequestDuplex readonly clone: () => Request }
```

**After**

```ts
export declare class Request extends BodyMixin { constructor (input: RequestInfo, init?: RequestInit) readonly cache: RequestCache readonly credentials: RequestCredentials readonly destination: RequestDestination readonly headers: Headers readonly integrity: string readonly method: string readonly mode: RequestMode readonly redirect: RequestRedirect readonly referrer: string readonly referrerPolicy: ReferrerPolicy readonly url: string readonly keepalive: boolean readonly signal: AbortSignal readonly duplex: RequestDuplex public clone (): Request }
```

#### `Undici.Response`

**Replacement:** `undici.Response`

Import Undici's named Response directly; clone is a method and Response.redirect status is optional in Undici 8.

**Before**

```ts
export declare class Response extends BodyMixin { constructor (body?: BodyInit, init?: ResponseInit) readonly headers: Headers readonly ok: boolean readonly status: number readonly statusText: string readonly type: ResponseType readonly url: string readonly redirected: boolean readonly clone: () => Response static error (): Response static json (data: any, init?: ResponseInit): Response static redirect (url: string | URL, status: ResponseRedirectStatus): Response }
```

**After**

```ts
export declare class Response extends BodyMixin { constructor (body?: BodyInit, init?: ResponseInit) readonly headers: Headers readonly ok: boolean readonly status: number readonly statusText: string readonly type: ResponseType readonly url: string readonly redirected: boolean public clone (): Response static error (): Response static json (data: any, init?: ResponseInit): Response static redirect (url: string | URL, status?: ResponseRedirectStatus): Response }
```

### `@effect/platform/Command`

#### `Command.Command`

**Replacement:** `ChildProcess.Command`

Commands moved to effect/unstable/process/ChildProcess and are now directly Effectable to spawn a ChildProcessHandle.

**Before**

```ts
export type Command = StandardCommand | PipedCommand;
export declare namespace Command { interface Proto extends Pipeable, Inspectable { readonly [CommandTypeId]: CommandTypeId; readonly _tag: string; } type Input = CommandInput; type Output = CommandOutput; }
```

#### `Command.Command.Input`

**Replacement:** `ChildProcess.CommandInput`

The standard-input configuration type was flattened out of the Command namespace.

**Before**

```ts
type Input = CommandInput;
```

#### `Command.Command.Proto`

**Replacement:** `ChildProcess.StandardCommand | ChildProcess.PipedCommand`

The public command prototype was removed; narrow the Command union to its StandardCommand or PipedCommand interfaces.

**Before**

```ts
interface Proto extends Pipeable, Inspectable { readonly [CommandTypeId]: CommandTypeId; readonly _tag: string; }
```

#### `Command.CommandTypeId`

**Replacement:** `none`

The command type-id alias is internal in v4; use ChildProcess.Command or ChildProcess.isCommand instead.

**Before**

```ts
export type CommandTypeId = typeof CommandTypeId;
```

#### `Command.env`

**Replacement:** `ChildProcess.setEnv`

Use the renamed command combinator.

**Before**

```ts
env: { (environment: Record<string, string | undefined>, options?: { readonly extendEnv?: boolean | undefined; }): (self: Command) => Command; (self: Command, environment: Record<string, string | undefined>, options?: { readonly extendEnv?: boolean | undefined; }): Command; }
```

#### `Command.exitCode`

**Replacement:** `ChildProcessSpawner.ChildProcessSpawner.exitCode`

Obtain the ChildProcessSpawner service and call exitCode, or spawn the Effectable command and read the handle exitCode.

**Before**

```ts
exitCode: (self: Command) => Effect<ExitCode, PlatformError, CommandExecutor>
```

#### `Command.feed`

**Replacement:** `ChildProcess.CommandOptions["stdin"]`

The feed combinator was removed; pass a Stream as stdin when constructing the command.

**Before**

```ts
feed: { (input: string): (self: Command) => Command; (self: Command, input: string): Command; }
```

#### `Command.flatten`

**Replacement:** `none`

No flatten helper remains; inspect StandardCommand and PipedCommand recursively when command structure is required.

**Before**

```ts
flatten: (self: Command) => NonEmptyReadonlyArray<StandardCommand>
```

#### `Command.lines`

**Replacement:** `ChildProcessSpawner.ChildProcessSpawner.lines`

Output collection moved onto the ChildProcessSpawner service.

**Before**

```ts
lines: (command: Command, encoding?: string) => Effect<Array<string>, PlatformError, CommandExecutor>
```

#### `Command.runInShell`

**Replacement:** `ChildProcess.CommandOptions["shell"]`

Set shell when calling ChildProcess.make; there is no post-construction shell combinator.

**Before**

```ts
runInShell: { (shell: string | boolean): (self: Command) => Command; (self: Command, shell: string | boolean): Command; }
```

#### `Command.start`

**Replacement:** `ChildProcessSpawner.ChildProcessSpawner.spawn`

Use the spawner service, or yield the Effectable ChildProcess.Command directly, to obtain a ChildProcessHandle.

**Before**

```ts
start: (command: Command) => Effect<Process, PlatformError, CommandExecutor | Scope>
```

#### `Command.stderr`

**Replacement:** `ChildProcess.CommandOptions["stderr"]`

Configure stderr in ChildProcess.make options; the standalone combinator was removed.

**Before**

```ts
stderr: { (stderr: Command.Output): (self: Command) => Command; (self: Command, stderr: Command.Output): Command; }
```

#### `Command.stdin`

**Replacement:** `ChildProcess.CommandOptions["stdin"]`

Configure stdin in ChildProcess.make options; the standalone combinator was removed.

**Before**

```ts
stdin: { (stdin: Command.Input): (self: Command) => Command; (self: Command, stdin: Command.Input): Command; }

[A["Encoded"]] extends [Readonly<Record<string, string | undefined>>] ? {} : `'UrlParams' kind can only be encoded to 'Record<string, string | undefined>'` : Kind extends "Uint8Array" ? [ A["Encoded"] ] extends [Uint8Array] ? {} : `'Uint8Array' kind can only be encoded to 'Uint8Array'` : Kind extends "Text" ? [A["Encoded"]] extends [string] ? {} : `'Text' kind can only be encoded to 'string'` : never; }

### `@effect/rpc/Rpc`

#### `Rpc.AddError`

**Replacement:** `effect/unstable/rpc/Rpc#AddError`

Retained; the added error must now be a Schema.Top and the resulting RPC also preserves its explicit service requirements.

**Before**

```ts
export type AddError<R extends Any, Error extends Schema.Schema.All> = R extends Rpc<infer _Tag, infer _Payload, infer _Success, infer _Error, infer _Middleware> ? Rpc<_Tag, _Payload, _Success, _Error | Error, _Middleware> : never;
```

#### `Rpc.AddMiddleware`

**Replacement:** `effect/unstable/rpc/Rpc#AddMiddleware`

Retained; middleware is now an RpcMiddleware.AnyService and its provides/requires metadata updates the RPC service requirements.

**Before**

```ts
export type AddMiddleware<R extends Any, Middleware extends RpcMiddleware.TagClassAny> = R extends Rpc<infer _Tag, infer _Payload, infer _Success, infer _Error, infer _Middleware> ? Rpc<_Tag, _Payload, _Success, _Error, _Middleware | Middleware> : never;
```

#### `Rpc.Any`

**Replacement:** `effect/unstable/rpc/Rpc#Any`

Retained as the erased RPC shape; use AnyWithProps when schema and middleware fields are required.

**Before**

```ts
export interface Any extends Pipeable { readonly [TypeId]: TypeId; readonly _tag: string; readonly key: string; }
```

#### `Rpc.AnySchema`

**Replacement:** `Schema.Top`

The RPC-specific erased schema alias was removed; use the v4 top schema constraint.

**Before**

```ts
export interface AnySchema extends Pipeable { readonly [Schema.TypeId]: any; readonly Type: any; readonly Encoded: any; readonly Context: any; readonly make?: (params: any, ...rest: ReadonlyArray<any>) => any; readonly ast: AST.AST; readonly annotations: any; }
```

#### `Rpc.AnyTaggedRequestSchema`

**Replacement:** `none`

RpcGroup no longer converts Schema.TaggedRequest classes into RPCs; declare the contract explicitly with Rpc.make.

**Before**

```ts
export interface AnyTaggedRequestSchema extends AnySchema { readonly _tag: string; readonly success: Schema.Schema.Any; readonly failure: Schema.Schema.All; }
```

#### `Rpc.Context`

**Replacement:** `effect/unstable/rpc/Rpc#Services`

Schema Context became decoding and encoding services; use Services, or ServicesClient / ServicesServer at the corresponding boundary.

**Before**

```ts
export type Context<R> = R extends Rpc<infer _Tag, infer _Payload, infer _Success, infer _Error, infer _Middleware> ? _Payload["Context"] | _Success["Context"] | _Error["Context"] : never;
```

#### `Rpc.Error`

**Replacement:** `effect/unstable/rpc/Rpc#Error`

Retained; it includes decoded errors contributed by attached middleware.

**Before**

```ts
export type Error<R> = Schema.Schema.Type<ErrorSchema<R>>;
```

#### `Rpc.ErrorEncoded`

**Replacement:** `Rpc.ErrorSchema<R>["Encoded"]`

The alias was removed; index the v4 error schema's Encoded member directly.

**Before**

```ts
export type ErrorEncoded<R> = Schema.Schema.Encoded<ErrorSchema<R>>;
```

#### `Rpc.ErrorExitEncoded`

**Replacement:** `Rpc.ErrorExitSchema<R>["Encoded"]`

Use the new exit error schema, which includes stream and middleware errors, then select its Encoded member.

**Before**

```ts
export type ErrorExitEncoded<R> = SuccessSchema<R> extends RpcSchema.Stream<infer _A, infer _E> ? _E["Encoded"] | ErrorEncoded<R> : ErrorEncoded<R>;
```

#### `Rpc.ErrorSchema`

**Replacement:** `effect/unstable/rpc/Rpc#ErrorSchema`

Retained; middleware errors now come from each service's error metadata.

**Before**

```ts
export type ErrorSchema<R> = R extends Rpc<infer _Tag, infer _Payload, infer _Success, infer _Error, infer _Middleware> ? _Error | _Middleware : never;
```

#### `Rpc.Handler`

**Replacement:** `effect/unstable/rpc/Rpc#Handler`

Retained; handler metadata now supplies ServerClient, RequestId, headers, and the concrete RPC.

**Before**

```ts
export interface Handler<Tag extends string> { readonly _: unique symbol; readonly tag: Tag; readonly handler: (request: any, options: { readonly clientId: number; readonly headers: Headers; }) => Effect<any, any> | Stream<any, any>; readonly context: Context<never>; }
```

#### `Rpc.Middleware`

**Replacement:** `effect/unstable/rpc/Rpc#Middleware`

Retained and extracts Context.Service identifiers from the attached middleware services.

**Before**

```ts
export type Middleware<R> = R extends Rpc<infer _Tag, infer _Payload, infer _Success, infer _Error, infer _Middleware> ? Context_.Tag.Identifier<_Middleware> : never;
```

#### `Rpc.MiddlewareClient`

**Replacement:** `effect/unstable/rpc/Rpc#MiddlewareClient`

Retained; required client middleware is derived from services configured with requiredForClient.

**Before**

```ts
export type MiddlewareClient<R> = R extends Rpc<infer _Tag, infer _Payload, infer _Success, infer _Error, infer _Middleware> ? _Middleware extends { readonly requiredForClient: true; } ? RpcMiddleware.ForClient<Context_.Tag.Identifier<_Middleware>> : never : never;
```

#### `Rpc.Payload`

**Replacement:** `effect/unstable/rpc/Rpc#Payload`

Retained as the decoded payload type; use PayloadConstructor for the input accepted by generated clients.

**Before**

```ts
export type Payload<R> = R extends Rpc<infer _Tag, infer _Payload, infer _Success, infer _Error, infer _Middleware> ? _Payload["Type"] : never;
```

#### `Rpc.Success`

**Replacement:** `effect/unstable/rpc/Rpc#Success`

Retained as the decoded success type.

```

#### `Rpc.SuccessChunkEncoded`

**Replacement:** `Rpc.SuccessExitSchema<R>["Encoded"]`

The alias was removed; for a streaming RPC the exit success schema is the stream element schema.

#### `Rpc.SuccessExitEncoded`

**Replacement:** `Rpc.SuccessExitSchema<R>["Encoded"]`

Use the new exit success schema and select its Encoded member; streaming RPC exits use the element schema separately from the terminal void exit.

#### `Rpc.SuccessSchema`

**Replacement:** `effect/unstable/rpc/Rpc#SuccessSchema`

Retained and uses the v4 Schema.Top constraint.

**Before**

#### `Rpc.Tag`

**Replacement:** `effect/unstable/rpc/Rpc#Tag`

Retained and also accounts for the v4 RPC service-requirement parameter.

```

#### `Rpc.TypeId`

**Replacement:** `none`

The RPC marker is private in v4; use Rpc.isRpc for runtime checks and Rpc.Any for type constraints.

**Before**

```ts

```

#### `Rpc.WrapperTypeId`

**Replacement:** `none`

The wrapper marker is private in v4; use Rpc.isWrapper and the public Wrapper type.

```

#### `Rpc.fromTaggedRequest`

**Replacement:** `Rpc.make`

Automatic TaggedRequest conversion was removed; pass the tag, payload, success, and error schemas explicitly to Rpc.make.

#### `Rpc.make`

**Replacement:** `effect/unstable/rpc/Rpc#make`

Retained; schemas use v4 Schema.Top constraints and the defect option accepts Rpc.DefectSchema.

**Before**

```ts
make: <const Tag extends string, Payload extends Schema.Schema.Any | Schema.Struct.Fields = typeof Schema.Void, Success extends Schema.Schema.Any = typeof Schema.Void, Error extends Schema.Schema.All = typeof Schema.Never, const Stream extends boolean = false>(tag: Tag, options?: { readonly payload?: Payload; readonly success?: Success; readonly error?: Error; readonly stream?: Stream; readonly defect?: Schema.Schema<unknown, any>; readonly primaryKey?: [Payload] extends [Schema.Struct.Fields] ? ((payload: Schema.Simplify<Schema.Struct.Type<NoInfer<Payload>>>) => string) : never; }) => Rpc<Tag, Payload extends Schema.Struct.Fields ? Schema.Struct<Payload> : Payload, Stream extends true ? RpcSchema.Stream<Success, Error> : Success, Stream extends true ? typeof Schema.Never : Error>
```

**After**

Either became Result in v4: migrate Left to Result.Failure, then use assertFailure; narrowed payload access changes from .left to .failure.

### `effect/Cache`

#### `Cache.Cache`

**Replacement:** `Cache.Cache`

The cache model remains, but v4 exposes a Pipeable value with explicit Cache operations and adds a lookup environment parameter.

**Before**

```ts
export declare namespace Cache { interface Variance<in out Key, in out Value, out Error> { readonly [CacheTypeId]: { readonly _Key: Types.Invariant<Key>; readonly _Error: Types.Covariant<Error>; readonly _Value: Types.Invariant<Value>; }; } interface ConsumerVariance<in out Key, out Value, out Error> { readonly [ConsumerCacheTypeId]: { readonly _Key: Types.Invariant<Key>; readonly _Error: Types.Covariant<Error>; readonly _Value: Types.Covariant<Value>; }; } }
```

**After**

```ts
export interface Cache<in out Key, in out A, in out E = never, out R = never> extends Pipeable { readonly [TypeId]: typeof TypeId; readonly map: MutableHashMap.MutableHashMap<Key, Entry<A, E>>; readonly capacity: number; readonly lookup: (key: Key) => Effect.Effect<A, E, R>; readonly timeToLive: (exit: Exit.Exit<A, E>, key: Key) => Duration.Duration; }
```

- `Cache.Cache.ConsumerVariance` -> `none`: The ConsumerCache view and its variance marker were removed; expose a narrower application interface around Cache operations when write access must be hidden.

#### `Cache.Cache.Variance`

**Replacement:** `none`

The public variance marker was removed; use Cache.Cache directly and do not depend on its branding internals.

**Before**

```ts
interface Variance<in out Key, in out Value, out Error> { readonly [CacheTypeId]: { readonly _Key: Types.Invariant<Key>; readonly _Error: Types.Covariant<Error>; readonly _Value: Types.Invariant<Value>; }; }
```

- `Cache.CacheStats` -> `none`: Built-in hit and miss statistics were removed; instrument the lookup and Cache.get calls explicitly, and use Cache.size for the current entry count.

#### `Cache.CacheTypeId`

**Replacement:** `none`

The cache type id is internal in v4; do not inspect or construct the cache brand directly.

**Before**

```ts

```

- `Cache.ConsumerCache` -> `Cache.Cache`: ConsumerCache was removed; use Cache.Cache and expose an application-defined read-only wrapper if capability restriction is required.

#### `Cache.ConsumerCacheTypeId`

**Replacement:** `none`

ConsumerCache and its type id were removed with the read-only cache view.

**Before**

```ts

```

- `Cache.EntryStats` -> `none`: Per-entry loaded-time statistics were removed; record lookup timing in application instrumentation if needed.

#### `Cache.Lookup`

**Replacement:** `(key: Key) => Effect.Effect<A, E, R>`

The named alias was removed; use an inline lookup function type or Cache.Cache<Key, A, E, R>["lookup"].

**Before**

```

#### `Cache.makeCacheStats`

**Replacement:** `none`

CacheStats and its constructor were removed; define an application metrics record if these counters are still required.

**Before**

**Replacement:** `none`

### `effect/Cause`

#### `Cause.Cause`

**Replacement:** `Cause.Cause`

The name remains, but v4 Cause<E> is a wrapper with readonly reasons: ReadonlyArray<Cause.Reason<E>>, not the v3 Empty/Fail/Die/Interrupt/Sequential/Parallel tree.

**Before**

```ts
export type Cause<E> = Empty | Fail<E> | Die | Interrupt | Sequential<E> | Parallel<E>;
export declare namespace Cause { interface Variance<out E> { readonly [CauseTypeId]: { readonly _E: Covariant<E>; }; } }
```

**After**

```ts
export interface Cause<out E> extends Pipeable, Inspectable, Equal { readonly [TypeId]: typeof TypeId; readonly reasons: ReadonlyArray<Reason<E>>; }
export declare namespace Cause { type Error<T> = T extends Cause<infer E> ? E : never; interface ReasonProto<Tag extends string> extends Inspectable, Equal { readonly [ReasonTypeId]: typeof ReasonTypeId; readonly _tag: Tag; readonly annotations: ReadonlyMap<string, unknown>; annotate(annotations: Context.Context<never> | ReadonlyMap<string, unknown>, options?: { readonly overwrite?: boolean | undefined; }): this; } }
```

#### `Cause.Cause.Variance`

**Replacement:** `none`

The public variance helper was removed. Cause.Cause is directly branded by Cause.TypeId; application code should not reproduce the old variance member.

**Before**

```ts

**Replacement:** `cause.reasons.reduce`

The six-case tree reducer type was removed with Empty, Sequential, and Parallel. Reduce the flat Reason array and switch on Fail, Die, or Interrupt instead.

```ts

```

#### `Cause.CauseTypeId`

**Replacement:** `Cause.TypeId`

The brand export is Cause.TypeId, a literal-string const. Use typeof Cause.TypeId in type positions; the v3 unique-symbol CauseTypeId alias is gone.

**Replacement:** `Cause.Die`

**Replacement:** `Cause.empty`

**Replacement:** `none`

**Replacement:** `Cause.UnknownError`

#### `Cause.UnknownExceptionTypeId`

**Replacement:** `Cause.UnknownErrorTypeId`

Rename the brand; v4 exports a literal-string const, so use typeof Cause.UnknownErrorTypeId in type positions.

#### `Cause.YieldableError`

**Replacement:** `Cause.YieldableError / Data.Error`

Cause.YieldableError remains as the interface/type, but its public constructor value was removed. Extend Data.Error for an untagged yieldable error or Data.TaggedError for a tagged one.

**Before**

**After**

```ts

```

**Replacement:** `Cause.fromReasons(self.reasons.flatMap(...))`

No direct v4 combinator. For each Fail reason, splice either f(reason.error).reasons or the constant cause's reasons; retain Die and Interrupt reasons, then rebuild with Cause.fromReasons.

**Before**

```ts
andThen: { <E, E2>(f: (e: E) => Cause<E2>): (self: Cause<E>) => Cause<E2>; <E2>(f: Cause<E2>): <E>(self: Cause<E>) => Cause<E2>; <E, E2>(self: Cause<E>, f: (e: E) => Cause<E2>): Cause<E2>; <E, E2>(self: Cause<E>, f: Cause<E2>): Cause<E2>; }

**Replacement:** `Cause.map(self, () => error)`

Use Cause.map with a constant function; only Fail errors change and Die/Interrupt reasons remain.

**Before**

```

**Replacement:** `Equal.equals(Cause.combine(self, that), self)`

There are no subtrees in v4. This tests whether all reasons from that are already present in self under v4 reason equality; use Equal.equals(self, that) when only whole-cause equality is intended.

**Before**

```ts

```

**Replacement:** `self.reasons.filter(Cause.isDieReason).map((reason) => reason.defect)`

Collect defect values from the flat Reason array. The result is a standard array rather than v3 Chunk.

**Before**

```ts

**Replacement:** `Cause.findErrorOption`

Direct Option-based replacement for extracting the first typed Fail error value.

**Replacement:** `Cause.findError`

Use the v4 Result-based split: success is the first E and failure is the original Cause<never> when no Fail reason exists.

**Replacement:** `self.reasons.filter(Cause.isFailReason).map((reason) => reason.error)`

Collect typed error values from the flat Reason array. The result is a standard array rather than v3 Chunk.

failures: <E>(self: Cause<E>) => Chunk.Chunk<E>

**Replacement:** `Cause.fromReasons(self.reasons.filter(...))`

**Before**

```ts

```

#### `Cause.find`

**Replacement:** `Option.firstSomeOf(self.reasons.map(...))`

No recursive nodes remain. Apply the partial function to Reason values and take the first Some, or use Cause.findFail/findError/findDie/findDefect/findInterrupt for standard searches.

**Before**

```ts
find: { <E, Z>(pf: (cause: Cause<E>) => Option.Option<Z>): (self: Cause<E>) => Option.Option<Z>; <E, Z>(self: Cause<E>, pf: (cause: Cause<E>) => Option.Option<Z>): Option.Option<Z>; }
```

#### `Cause.flatMap`

**Replacement:** `Cause.fromReasons(self.reasons.flatMap((reason) => Cause.isFailReason(reason) ? f(reason.error).reasons : [reason]))`

No direct v4 export. Flat-map only Fail reasons into replacement causes, preserve Die/Interrupt reasons, and rebuild from the resulting Reason array.

**Before**

```ts
flatMap: { <E, E2>(f: (e: E) => Cause<E2>): (self: Cause<E>) => Cause<E2>; <E, E2>(self: Cause<E>, f: (e: E) => Cause<E2>): Cause<E2>; }
```

#### `Cause.flatten`

**Replacement:** `Cause.fromReasons(self.reasons.flatMap((reason) => Cause.isFailReason(reason) ? reason.error.reasons : [reason]))`

No direct v4 export. For Cause<Cause<E>>, splice each Fail reason's nested cause.reasons and retain Die/Interrupt reasons.

**Before**

```ts
flatten: <E>(self: Cause<Cause<E>>) => Cause<E>
```

#### `Cause.flipCauseOption`

**Replacement:** `Cause.fromReasons + Option`

Rewrite over reasons: drop Fail(None), replace Fail(Some(e)) with Cause.makeFailReason(e), retain Die/Interrupt, then return None only when a non-empty input loses every reason; preserve Some(Cause.empty) for an empty input.

**Before**

```ts
flipCauseOption: <E>(self: Cause<Option.Option<E>>) => Option.Option<Cause<E>>
```

#### `Cause.interruptOption`

**Replacement:** `Cause.findInterrupt`

The replacement returns Result.Result<Cause.Interrupt, Cause.Cause<E>> rather than Option<FiberId>; on success read reason.fiberId, now number | undefined.

**Before**

```ts
interruptOption: <E>(self: Cause<E>) => Option.Option<FiberId.FiberId>
```

#### `Cause.isDie`

**Replacement:** `Cause.hasDies`

Use the v4 cause-level predicate for the presence of at least one Die reason.

**Before**

```ts
isDie: <E>(self: Cause<E>) => boolean
```

#### `Cause.isDieType`

**Replacement:** `Cause.isDieReason`

Apply this guard to an entry of cause.reasons; Cause itself is no longer a Die union variant.

**Before**

```ts
isDieType: <E>(self: Cause<E>) => self is Die
```

#### `Cause.isEmpty`

**Replacement:** `self.reasons.length === 0`

V4 represents an empty cause with an empty reasons array and exports no isEmpty function.

**Before**

```ts
isEmpty: <E>(self: Cause<E>) => boolean
```

#### `Cause.isEmptyType`

**Replacement:** `self.reasons.length === 0`

The check remains possible, but there is no Empty subtype to narrow to because v4 Cause is not a variant union.

**Before**

```ts
isEmptyType: <E>(self: Cause<E>) => self is Empty
```

#### `Cause.isExceededCapacityException`

**Replacement:** `Cause.isExceededCapacityError`

Rename the guard along with ExceededCapacityError.

**Before**

```ts
isExceededCapacityException: (u: unknown) => u is ExceededCapacityException
```

#### `Cause.isFailType`

**Replacement:** `Cause.isFailReason`

Apply this guard to an entry of cause.reasons; Cause itself is no longer a Fail union variant.

**Before**

```ts
isFailType: <E>(self: Cause<E>) => self is Fail<E>
```

#### `Cause.isFailure`

**Replacement:** `Cause.hasFails`

Use the v4 cause-level predicate for the presence of at least one Fail reason.

**Before**

```ts
isFailure: <E>(self: Cause<E>) => boolean
```

#### `Cause.isIllegalArgumentException`

**Replacement:** `Cause.isIllegalArgumentError`

Rename the guard along with IllegalArgumentError.

**Before**

```ts
isIllegalArgumentException: (u: unknown) => u is IllegalArgumentException
```

#### `Cause.isInterruptType`

**Replacement:** `Cause.isInterruptReason`

Apply this guard to an entry of cause.reasons; Cause itself is no longer an Interrupt union variant.

**Before**

```ts
isInterruptType: <E>(self: Cause<E>) => self is Interrupt
```

#### `Cause.isInterrupted`

**Replacement:** `Cause.hasInterrupts`

Use the v4 cause-level predicate for the presence of at least one Interrupt reason.

**Before**

```ts
isInterrupted: <E>(self: Cause<E>) => boolean
```

#### `Cause.isInterruptedException`

**Replacement:** `none`

No v4 InterruptError class or unknown-value guard is exported. When the Cause is available, test Cause.hasInterruptsOnly before squashing or rendering it.

**Before**

```ts
isInterruptedException: (u: unknown) => u is InterruptedException
```

#### `Cause.isInterruptedOnly`

**Replacement:** `Cause.hasInterruptsOnly`

Direct cause-level rename; it is false for Cause.empty and true only when at least one reason exists and every reason is Interrupt.

**Before**

```ts
isInterruptedOnly: <E>(self: Cause<E>) => boolean
```

#### `Cause.isNoSuchElementException`

**Replacement:** `Cause.isNoSuchElementError`

Rename the guard along with NoSuchElementError.

**Before**

```ts
isNoSuchElementException: (u: unknown) => u is NoSuchElementException
```

#### `Cause.isParallelType`

**Replacement:** `none`

Parallel cause nodes were removed; v4 stores all reasons in one flat array and does not retain composition kind.

**Before**

```ts
isParallelType: <E>(self: Cause<E>) => self is Parallel<E>
```

#### `Cause.isRuntimeException`

**Replacement:** `none`

RuntimeException and its brand were removed. Use instanceof Error for generic errors or define a Data.Error/Data.TaggedError class with its own guard when nominal recognition is required.

**Before**

```ts
isRuntimeException: (u: unknown) => u is RuntimeException
```

#### `Cause.isSequentialType`

**Replacement:** `none`

Sequential cause nodes were removed; v4 stores all reasons in one flat array and does not retain composition kind.

**Before**

```ts
isSequentialType: <E>(self: Cause<E>) => self is Sequential<E>
```

#### `Cause.isTimeoutException`

**Replacement:** `Cause.isTimeoutError`

Rename the guard along with TimeoutError.

**Before**

```ts
isTimeoutException: (u: unknown) => u is TimeoutException
```

#### `Cause.isUnknownException`

**Replacement:** `Cause.isUnknownError`

Rename the guard along with UnknownError.

**Before**

```ts
isUnknownException: (u: unknown) => u is UnknownException
```

- `Cause.keepDefects` -> `Cause.fromReasons(self.reasons.filter(Cause.isDieReason))`: Keep every Die reason, not merely the first defect. Return Option.none when the filtered array is empty and Option.some of the rebuilt cause otherwise; Cause.findDefect alone is not behaviorally equivalent.

#### `Cause.linearize`

**Replacement:** `self.reasons`

No direct replacement: v4 discarded sequential/parallel structure, so there are no parallel branches to linearize. Rewrite the consumer to process the flat Reason array.

**Before**

```ts
linearize: <E>(self: Cause<E>) => HashSet.HashSet<Cause<E>>
```

#### `Cause.originalError`

**Replacement:** `Function.identity`

V3 used this to unwrap span-capture proxies. V4 stores tracing data on Reason.annotations and no longer proxies errors, so the input is already the original value.

**Before**

```ts
originalError: <E>(obj: E) => E
```

#### `Cause.parallel`

**Replacement:** `Cause.combine`

Combine the two flat reason arrays; v4 intentionally no longer records whether composition was parallel or sequential.

**Before**

```ts
parallel: <E, E2>(left: Cause<E>, right: Cause<E2>) => Cause<E | E2>
```

#### `Cause.reduce`

**Replacement:** `self.reasons.reduce`

Reduce the flat Reason array directly. The callback now sees only Fail, Die, and Interrupt reasons, never Empty or composition nodes.

**Before**

```ts
reduce: { <Z, E>(zero: Z, pf: (accumulator: Z, cause: Cause<E>) => Option.Option<Z>): (self: Cause<E>) => Z; <Z, E>(self: Cause<E>, zero: Z, pf: (accumulator: Z, cause: Cause<E>) => Option.Option<Z>): Z; }
```

#### `Cause.reduceWithContext`

**Replacement:** `self.reasons.reduce`

Capture the context in the reducer closure and reduce the flat Reason array; sequentialCase and parallelCase have no v4 analogue.

**Before**

```ts
reduceWithContext: { <C, E, Z>(context: C, reducer: CauseReducer<C, E, Z>): (self: Cause<E>) => Z; <C, E, Z>(self: Cause<E>, context: C, reducer: CauseReducer<C, E, Z>): Z; }
```

#### `Cause.sequential`

**Replacement:** `Cause.combine`

Combine the two flat reason arrays; v4 intentionally no longer records whether composition was parallel or sequential.

**Before**

```ts
sequential: <E, E2>(left: Cause<E>, right: Cause<E2>) => Cause<E | E2>
```

#### `Cause.size`

**Replacement:** `self.reasons.length`

The v3 node count becomes the number of flat reasons in v4.

**Before**

```ts
size: <E>(self: Cause<E>) => number
```

#### `Cause.squashWith`

**Replacement:** `Result.match(Cause.findError(self), { onSuccess: f, onFailure: Cause.squash })`

Apply f only to the first typed Fail error; if no Fail exists, squash the returned Cause<never>. This preserves v3's priority and avoids evaluating f for later Fail reasons.

**Before**

```ts
squashWith: { <E>(f: (error: E) => unknown): (self: Cause<E>) => unknown; <E>(self: Cause<E>, f: (error: E) => unknown): unknown; }
```

#### `Cause.stripFailures`

**Replacement:** `Cause.fromReasons(self.reasons.filter((reason) => !Cause.isFailReason(reason)))`

Remove Fail reasons and retain Die plus Interrupt reasons, then rebuild the cause. The v3 prose saying interrupts were removed did not match its implementation.

**Before**

```ts
stripFailures: <E>(self: Cause<E>) => Cause<never>
```

#### `Cause.stripSomeDefects`

**Replacement:** `Cause.fromReasons + Option`

Filter out each Die reason for which pf(reason.defect) is Some, retain all other reasons, and rebuild. Return None only when a non-empty input loses every reason; preserve Some(Cause.empty) for empty input.

**Before**

```ts
stripSomeDefects: { (pf: (defect: unknown) => Option.Option<unknown>): <E>(self: Cause<E>) => Option.Option<Cause<E>>; <E>(self: Cause<E>, pf: (defect: unknown) => Option.Option<unknown>): Option.Option<Cause<E>>; }
```

#### `Channel.Channel`

**Replacement:** `Channel.Channel`

Retained, but reorder type parameters from <OutElem, InElem, OutErr, InErr, OutDone, InDone, Env> to <OutElem, OutErr, OutDone, InElem, InErr, InDone, Env>. Convert Effect values explicitly with Channel.fromEffect or Channel.fromEffectDone.

**Before**

```ts

```

**After**

```ts

**Replacement:** `Channel.ChannelUnify`

#### `Channel.foldChannel`

**Replacement:** `none`

V4 has no exact two-sided fold over failure and completion. Use catchCause or catch for failure-only handling, concatWith for success-only handling, or match the Pull in a custom transform.

**Before**

```ts

#### `Channel.fromEither`

**Replacement:** `Channel.fromEffectDone`

Either is now Result. Use Channel.fromEffectDone(Effect.fromResult(result)) to preserve success as the done value.

**Before**

```ts
fromEither: <R, L>(either: Either.Either<R, L>) => Channel<never, unknown, L, unknown, R, unknown>
```

#### `Channel.fromInput`

**Replacement:** `none`

SingleProducerAsyncInput was removed. Model the producer with Queue and Pull; use Channel.fromPull with Queue.take when a typed done value matters.

**Before**

```ts
fromInput: <Err, Elem, Done>(input: SingleProducerAsyncInput.AsyncInputConsumer<Err, Elem, Done>) => Channel<Elem, unknown, Err, unknown, Done, unknown>
```

#### `Channel.fromOption`

**Replacement:** `Channel.fromEffectDone`

Use Channel.fromEffectDone(Effect.fromOption(option, Option.none)) to preserve the v3 Option.none error, or omit onNone for the v4 NoSuchElementError default.

**Before**

```ts
fromOption: <A>(option: Option.Option<A>) => Channel<never, unknown, Option.Option<never>, unknown, A, unknown>
```

**Replacement:** `Channel.fromPubSubTake`

Change the protocol to PubSub<Take<Elem, Err, Done>> and use Channel.flattenArray(Channel.fromPubSubTake(pubsub)). The v4 constructor owns the scoped subscription and returns a Channel directly.

**Replacement:** `none`

The channel instruction AST was removed. Implement a one-step upstream read with Channel.fromTransform and Pull matching, including Cause.Done handling.

**Before**

```ts

#### `Channel.readWithCause`

**Replacement:** `none`

The channel instruction AST was removed. Implement a one-step upstream read with Channel.fromTransform and Pull matching, including Cause.Done handling.

**Before**

```ts
readWithCause: <InElem, OutElem, OutErr, InErr, OutDone, InDone, Env, OutElem2, OutErr2, OutDone2, Env2, OutElem3, OutErr3, OutDone3, Env3>(options: { readonly onInput: (input: InElem) => Channel<OutElem, InElem, OutErr, InErr, OutDone, InDone, Env>; readonly onFailure: (cause: Cause.Cause<InErr>) => Channel<OutElem2, InElem, OutErr2, InErr, OutDone2, InDone, Env2>; readonly onDone: (done: InDone) => Channel<OutElem3, InElem, OutErr3, InErr, OutDone3, InDone, Env3>; }) => Channel<OutElem | OutElem2 | OutElem3, InElem, OutErr | OutErr2 | OutErr3, InErr, OutDone | OutDone2 | OutDone3, InDone, Env | Env2 | Env3>

#### `Channel.run`

**Replacement:** `Channel.runDone`

Renamed to runDone for an inputless, outputless channel. Use runDrain if emitted elements should be discarded.

**Before**

```ts
run: <OutErr, InErr, OutDone, InDone, Env>(self: Channel<never, unknown, OutErr, InErr, OutDone, InDone, Env>) => Effect.Effect<OutDone, OutErr, Env>
```

#### `Channel.runScoped`

**Replacement:** `Channel.toPull`

No direct scoped runner remains. Use toPull in the caller scope and recover Cause.Done; use runDone or runDrain when an internally managed scope is acceptable.

**Before**

```ts

```

#### `Channel.scopedWith`

**Replacement:** `Channel.unwrap`

Use Channel.unwrap(Effect.map(Effect.scope, (scope) => Channel.fromEffect(f(scope)))) so the effect uses the active channel scope.

**Before**

```ts

```

#### `Channel.toPullIn`

**Replacement:** `Channel.toPullScoped`

Renamed to toPullScoped. The returned Pull emits elements directly and represents completion with Cause.Done instead of Either.

**Before**

```ts

```

#### `Channel.toSink`

**Replacement:** `Sink.fromChannel`

Constructor moved to Sink. Adapt the channel to non-empty array input, no emitted leftovers, and a Sink.End done value.

**Before**

```ts

```

#### `Channel.toStream`

**Replacement:** `Stream.fromChannel`

Constructor moved to Stream. Adapt Chunk outputs to non-empty readonly arrays and map the channel done value to void.

**Before**

```ts

```

#### `Channel.unwrapScoped`

**Replacement:** `Channel.unwrap`

Use unwrap; v4 supplies the active channel scope to the effect and removes Scope from the resulting requirement.

**Before**

```ts

#### `Channel.unwrapScopedWith`

**Replacement:** `Channel.unwrap`

Use Channel.unwrap(Effect.flatMap(Effect.scope, f)) to pass the active channel scope to f.

**Before**

```ts

```

**Replacement:** `Channel.succeed`

Renamed to succeed, which emits one element in v4. Use Channel.end when migrating v3 succeed, which produced a done value.

```ts

**Replacement:** `Channel.fromArray`

#### `Channel.zip`

**Replacement:** `Channel.concatWith`

For sequential zip, concatWith the left channel and mapDone the right result to a tuple. Concurrent tuple-done semantics require custom Pull coordination.

**Before**

```ts

```

#### `Channel.zipLeft`

**Replacement:** `Channel.concatWith`

For sequential zipLeft, concatWith and mapDone the right result back to the left done value. Concurrent done preservation requires custom Pull coordination.

**Before**

```ts

### `effect/ConfigError`

#### `ConfigError.And`

**Replacement:** `SchemaIssue.Composite`

The ConfigError boolean ADT was removed; combined schema failures are represented inside Config.ConfigError.cause as SchemaIssue.Composite.

**Before**

```ts

```

#### `ConfigError.ConfigError`

**Replacement:** `Config.ConfigError`

Config errors are now a class in effect/Config wrapping either ConfigProvider.SourceError or Schema.SchemaError.

**Before**

```ts
export type ConfigError = And | Or | InvalidData | MissingData | SourceUnavailable | Unsupported;
export declare namespace ConfigError { interface Proto { readonly _tag: "ConfigError"; readonly [ConfigErrorTypeId]: ConfigErrorTypeId; } type Reducer<C, Z> = ConfigErrorReducer<C, Z>; }
```

#### `ConfigError.ConfigError.Proto`

**Replacement:** `Config.ConfigError`

The public prototype interface was removed; use the Config.ConfigError class.

**Before**

```ts
interface Proto { readonly _tag: "ConfigError"; readonly [ConfigErrorTypeId]: ConfigErrorTypeId; }
```

#### `ConfigError.ConfigError.Reducer`

**Replacement:** `none`

The ConfigError-specific reducer API was removed; inspect ConfigError.cause and recurse over SchemaError.issue when structured handling is required.

**Before**

```ts
type Reducer<C, Z> = ConfigErrorReducer<C, Z>;
```

#### `ConfigError.ConfigErrorReducer`

**Replacement:** `none`

The ConfigError-specific reducer API was removed; inspect ConfigError.cause and recurse over SchemaError.issue when structured handling is required.

**Before**

```ts
export interface ConfigErrorReducer<in C, in out Z> { andCase(context: C, left: Z, right: Z): Z; orCase(context: C, left: Z, right: Z): Z; invalidDataCase(context: C, path: Array<string>, message: string): Z; missingDataCase(context: C, path: Array<string>, message: string): Z; sourceUnavailableCase(context: C, path: Array<string>, message: string, cause: Cause.Cause<unknown>): Z; unsupportedCase(context: C, path: Array<string>, message: string): Z; }
```

#### `ConfigError.ConfigErrorTypeId`

**Replacement:** `error instanceof Config.ConfigError`

The marker is gone because ConfigError is a class in v4.

**Before**

```

#### `ConfigError.InvalidData`

**Replacement:** `new Config.ConfigError(new Schema.SchemaError(issue))`

Invalid configuration is now expressed as a SchemaIssue wrapped by SchemaError and Config.ConfigError.

**Before**

```ts

```

#### `ConfigError.MissingData`

**Replacement:** `new Config.ConfigError(new Schema.SchemaError(new SchemaIssue.MissingKey(...)))`

Missing configuration is represented by Schema issues, commonly MissingKey under one or more Pointer nodes.

**Before**

```ts
export interface MissingData extends ConfigError.Proto { readonly _op: "MissingData"; readonly path: Array<string>; readonly message: string; }
```

#### `ConfigError.Options`

**Replacement:** `none`

The shared constructor options type was removed; ConfigProvider.SourceError accepts message and optional cause, while Schema issues have issue-specific constructors.

**Before**

```ts
export interface Options { readonly pathDelim: string; }
```

#### `ConfigError.Or`

**Replacement:** `SchemaIssue.AnyOf`

The ConfigError boolean ADT was removed; alternative schema failures are represented inside Config.ConfigError.cause as SchemaIssue.AnyOf.

**Before**

```ts
export interface Or extends ConfigError.Proto { readonly _op: "Or"; readonly left: ConfigError; readonly right: ConfigError; readonly message: string; }
```

#### `ConfigError.SourceUnavailable`

**Replacement:** `new ConfigProvider.SourceError({ message, cause })`

Source failures moved to effect/ConfigProvider and are wrapped by Config.ConfigError when a Config is parsed.

**Before**

```ts
export interface SourceUnavailable extends ConfigError.Proto { readonly _op: "SourceUnavailable"; readonly path: Array<string>; readonly message: string; readonly cause: Cause.Cause<unknown>; }
```

#### `ConfigError.Unsupported`

**Replacement:** `none`

The variant was removed; use a SchemaError for unsupported input or ConfigProvider.SourceError for source capability failures.

**Before**

```ts
export interface Unsupported extends ConfigError.Proto { readonly _op: "Unsupported"; readonly path: Array<string>; readonly message: string; }
```

#### `ConfigError.isAnd`

**Replacement:** `error.cause.issue._tag === "Composite"`

After narrowing cause with Schema.isSchemaError, inspect the SchemaIssue tag; the old And node no longer exists.

**Before**

```ts
isAnd: (self: ConfigError) => self is And
```

#### `ConfigError.isConfigError`

**Replacement:** `error instanceof Config.ConfigError`

ConfigError is a class in v4.

**Before**

```ts

```

#### `ConfigError.isInvalidData`

**Replacement:** `Schema.isSchemaError(error.cause)`

Parsing and validation failures are SchemaError causes; inspect the contained SchemaIssue for finer classification.

**Before**

```ts

```

#### `ConfigError.isMissingData`

**Replacement:** `Schema.isSchemaError(error.cause)`

After narrowing to SchemaError, recursively inspect MissingKey, absent InvalidType/InvalidValue, Pointer, and aggregate issues; there is no public one-step guard.

**Before**

```ts

#### `ConfigError.isMissingDataOnly`

**Before**

#### `ConfigError.isOr`

**Replacement:** `error.cause.issue._tag === "AnyOf"`

After narrowing cause with Schema.isSchemaError, inspect the SchemaIssue tag; the old Or node no longer exists.

**Before**

```ts
isOr: (self: ConfigError) => self is Or
```

#### `ConfigError.isSourceUnavailable`

**Replacement:** `error.cause instanceof ConfigProvider.SourceError`

Provider source failures now use the ConfigProvider.SourceError class.

**Before**

```ts

```

#### `ConfigError.isUnsupported`

**Replacement:** `none`

The Unsupported variant was removed; report unsupported custom decoding through a SchemaError or source failures through ConfigProvider.SourceError.

**Before**

```ts

```

#### `ConfigError.prefixed`

**Replacement:** `SchemaIssue.Pointer`

Represent path context by wrapping the underlying SchemaIssue in a Pointer before constructing SchemaError.

**Before**

```ts

#### `ConfigError.reduceWithContext`

**Replacement:** `none`

The specialized fold was removed; branch on ConfigError.cause, then recurse over the public SchemaIssue union if a fold is needed.

**Before**

```ts

**Replacement:** `none`

```

**After**

```ts
export interface Console { assert(condition: boolean, ...args: ReadonlyArray<any>): void; clear(): void; count(label?: string): void; countReset(label?: string): void; debug(...args: ReadonlyArray<any>): void; dir(item: any, options?: any): void; dirxml(...args: ReadonlyArray<any>): void; error(...args: ReadonlyArray<any>): void; group(...args: ReadonlyArray<any>): void; groupCollapsed(...args: ReadonlyArray<any>): void; groupEnd(): void; info(...args: ReadonlyArray<any>): void; log(...args: ReadonlyArray<any>): void; table(tabularData: any, properties?: ReadonlyArray<string>): void; time(label?: string): void; timeEnd(label?: string): void; timeLog(label?: string, ...args: ReadonlyArray<any>): void; trace(...args: ReadonlyArray<any>): void; warn(...args: ReadonlyArray<any>): void; }

```

#### `Console.UnsafeConsole`

**Replacement:** `Console.Console`

```ts
export interface UnsafeConsole { assert(condition: boolean, ...args: ReadonlyArray<any>): void; clear(): void; count(label?: string): void; countReset(label?: string): void; debug(...args: ReadonlyArray<any>): void; dir(item: any, options?: any): void; dirxml(...args: ReadonlyArray<any>): void; error(...args: ReadonlyArray<any>): void; group(...args: ReadonlyArray<any>): void; groupCollapsed(...args: ReadonlyArray<any>): void; groupEnd(): void; info(...args: ReadonlyArray<any>): void; log(...args: ReadonlyArray<any>): void; table(tabularData: any, properties?: ReadonlyArray<string>): void; time(label?: string): void; timeEnd(label?: string): void; timeLog(label?: string, ...args: ReadonlyArray<any>): void; trace(...args: ReadonlyArray<any>): void; warn(...args: ReadonlyArray<any>): void; }

```

**After**

```ts

#### `Context.Reference`

**Replacement:** `Context.Reference<Shape>`

```

**Replacement:** `Context.Reference<Shape>(id, { defaultValue })`

```

**Replacement:** `none`

**Replacement:** `Context.ServiceClass<Self, Id, Shape>`

```

#### `Context.TagTypeId`

Zoned : Utc; type Unit = UnitSingular | UnitPlural; type UnitSingular = "milli" | "second" | "minute" | "hour" | "day" | "week" | "month" | "year"; type UnitPlural = "millis" | "seconds" | "minutes" | "hours" | "days" | "weeks" | "months" | "years"; interface PartsWithWeekday { readonly millis: number; readonly seconds: number; readonly minutes: number; readonly hours: number; readonly day: number; readonly weekDay: number; readonly month: number; readonly year: number; } interface Parts { readonly millis: number; readonly seconds: number; readonly minutes: number; readonly hours: number; readonly day: number; readonly month: number; readonly year: number; } interface PartsForMath { readonly millis: number; readonly seconds: number; readonly minutes: number; readonly hours: number; readonly days: number; readonly weeks: number; readonly months: number; readonly years: number; } interface Proto extends Pipeable, Inspectable { readonly [TypeId]: TypeId; } }

Zoned : Utc; type Unit = UnitSingular | UnitPlural; type UnitSingular = "millisecond" | "second" | "minute" | "hour" | "day" | "week" | "month" | "year"; type UnitPlural = "milliseconds" | "seconds" | "minutes" | "hours" | "days" | "weeks" | "months" | "years"; interface PartsWithWeekday { readonly millisecond: number; readonly second: number; readonly minute: number; readonly hour: number; readonly day: number; readonly weekDay: number; readonly month: number; readonly year: number; } interface Parts { readonly millisecond: number; readonly second: number; readonly minute: number; readonly hour: number; readonly day: number; readonly month: number; readonly year: number; } interface PartsForMath { readonly milliseconds: number; readonly seconds: number; readonly minutes: number; readonly hours: number; readonly days: number; readonly weeks: number; readonly months: number; readonly years: number; } interface Instant { readonly epochMilliseconds: number; } interface InstantWithZone { readonly timeZoneId: string; readonly epochMilliseconds: number; } interface Proto extends Pipeable, Inspectable { readonly [TypeId]: typeof TypeId; } }

#### `Deferred.Deferred`

**Replacement:** `Deferred.Deferred`

The model remains but is now Pipeable rather than an Effect subtype; replace yielding the Deferred itself with Deferred.await.

**Before**

```ts

```

**After**

```ts

export declare namespace Deferred { interface Variance<in out A, in out E> { readonly [TypeId]: { readonly _A: Types.Invariant<A>; readonly _E: Types.Invariant<E>; }; } }
```

#### `Deferred.Deferred.Variance`

**Replacement:** `Deferred.Deferred.Variance`

The marker remains under Deferred.Deferred, but its brand uses an internal type id; ordinary code should use Deferred.Deferred directly.

**Before**

```ts
interface Variance<in out A, in out E> { readonly [DeferredTypeId]: { readonly _A: Types.Invariant<A>; readonly _E: Types.Invariant<E>; }; }
```

**After**

```ts
interface Variance<in out A, in out E> { readonly [TypeId]: { readonly _A: Types.Invariant<A>; readonly _E: Types.Invariant<E>; }; }
```

#### `Deferred.DeferredTypeId`

**Replacement:** `none`

The Deferred type id is internal in v4; do not inspect or construct the brand directly.

**Before**

```ts

```

#### `Deferred.DeferredUnify`

**Replacement:** `none`

Deferred is no longer an Effect subtype, so its Effect unification helper was removed; call Deferred.await explicitly.

**Before**

```ts
export interface DeferredUnify<A extends { [Unify.typeSymbol]?: any; }> extends Effect.EffectUnify<A> { Deferred?: () => Extract<A[Unify.typeSymbol], Deferred<any, any>>; }
```

#### `Deferred.DeferredUnifyIgnore`

**Replacement:** `none`

Deferred is no longer an Effect subtype, so its Effect unification ignore marker was removed.

**Before**

```ts

```

#### `Deferred.await`

**Replacement:** `Deferred.await`

The function remains; call it explicitly because Deferred is no longer an Effect subtype in v4.

**Before**

```ts
_await: <A, E>(self: Deferred<A, E>) => Effect.Effect<A, E>
```

**After**

```ts
_await: <A, E>(self: Deferred<A, E>) => Effect<A, E>
```

- `Deferred.makeAs` -> `Deferred.makeUnsafe`: Use the synchronous v4 constructor; it no longer accepts or records a FiberId.

#### `Deferred.poll`

**Replacement:** `Deferred.poll`

The function remains and returns an Option containing the stored completion Effect.

**Before**

```ts

**After**

```ts
export declare function poll<A, E>(self: Deferred<A, E>): Effect<Option.Option<Effect<A, E>>>;
```

**Replacement:** `Deferred.doneUnsafe`

The unsafe suffix moved to the end; the v4 function returns whether this call completed the Deferred.

**Before**

**Replacement:** `Deferred.makeUnsafe`
