- `RuntimeFlags.disableCooperativeYielding` -> `Effect.provideService(References.PreventSchedulerYield, true)`: Prevent scheduler yielding through its Context.Reference.

- `RuntimeFlags.disableInterruption` -> `Effect.uninterruptible`: Use an uninterruptible region instead of changing a runtime flag.

- `RuntimeFlags.disableOpSupervision` -> `none`: Operation supervision and its runtime flag were removed.

- `RuntimeFlags.disableRuntimeMetrics` -> `Metric.disableRuntimeMetrics`: Disable fiber runtime metrics directly; use disableRuntimeMetricsLayer when providing a Layer.

- `RuntimeFlags.disableWindDown` -> `none`: The wind-down flag is runtime-internal in v4; use normal scoped finalizers and explicit interruptibility regions.

#### `RuntimeFlags.enable`

**Replacement:** `none`

The generic flag operation was removed; enable the corresponding behavior directly.

**Before**

```ts
enable: { (flag: RuntimeFlag): (self: RuntimeFlags) => RuntimeFlags; (self: RuntimeFlags, flag: RuntimeFlag): RuntimeFlags; }
```

#### `RuntimeFlags.enableAll`

**Replacement:** `none`

The aggregate flags value was removed; configure scheduler yielding, interruptibility, and metrics independently.

**Before**

```ts
enableAll: { (flags: RuntimeFlags): (self: RuntimeFlags) => RuntimeFlags; (self: RuntimeFlags, flags: RuntimeFlags): RuntimeFlags; }
```

- `RuntimeFlags.enableCooperativeYielding` -> `Effect.provideService(References.PreventSchedulerYield, false)`: Allow scheduler yielding through its Context.Reference.

- `RuntimeFlags.enableInterruption` -> `Effect.interruptible`: Use an interruptible region instead of changing a runtime flag.

- `RuntimeFlags.enableOpSupervision` -> `none`: Operation supervision and its runtime flag were removed.

- `RuntimeFlags.enableRuntimeMetrics` -> `Metric.enableRuntimeMetrics`: Enable fiber runtime metrics directly; use enableRuntimeMetricsLayer when providing a Layer.

- `RuntimeFlags.enableWindDown` -> `none`: The wind-down flag is runtime-internal in v4; use normal scoped finalizers and explicit interruptibility regions.

#### `STM.All.IsDiscard`

**Replacement:** `Effect.All.IsDiscard`

The helper moved to Effect.All because STM.all is now Effect.all.

**Before**

```ts
type IsDiscard<A> = [Extract<A, { readonly discard: true; }>] extends [never] ? false : true;
```

#### `STM.All.Narrow`

**Replacement:** `none`

Effect.all uses a const generic directly, so the separate tuple-narrowing helper was removed.

**Before**

```ts
type Narrow<A> = (A extends [] ? [] : never) | A;
```

#### `STM.All.Options`

**Replacement:** `none`

Effect.all inlines its options type; use its concurrency, discard, and mode options directly.

**Before**

```ts
type Options = { readonly discard?: boolean | undefined; };
```

#### `STM.All.STMAny`

**Replacement:** `Effect.All.EffectAny`

STM inputs are ordinary Effects in v4, so use the Effect.All helper.

**Before**

```ts
type STMAny = STM<any, any, any>;
```

#### `STM.All.Signature`

**Replacement:** `typeof Effect.all`

The named STM all signature was removed; refer to Effect.all directly.

**Before**

```ts
interface Signature { <Arg extends ReadonlyArray<STMAny> | Iterable<STMAny> | Record<string, STMAny>, O extends NoExcessProperties<Options, O>>(arg: Narrow<Arg>, options?: O): [Arg] extends [ReadonlyArray<STMAny>] ? ReturnTuple<Arg, IsDiscard<O>> : [Arg] extends [Iterable<STMAny>] ? ReturnIterable<Arg, IsDiscard<O>> : [Arg] extends [Record<string, STMAny>] ? ReturnObject<Arg, IsDiscard<O>> : never; }
```

#### `STM.Do`

**Replacement:** `Effect.Do`

The combinator keeps its name, but STM values are now ordinary Effects. Run the complete transaction with Effect.tx. V4 Tx operations return ordinary Effects; compose multiple operations under one outer Effect.tx to keep them atomic.

**Before**

```ts
Do: STM<{}>
```

#### `STM.STM`

**Replacement:** `Effect.Effect`

The distinct STM instruction type was removed. Tx APIs return Effect values; wrap the complete transaction in Effect.tx.

**Before**

```ts
export interface STM<out A, out E = never, out R = never> extends Effect.Effect<A, E, R>, STM.Variance<A, E, R>, Pipeable { [Unify.typeSymbol]?: unknown; [Unify.unifySymbol]?: STMUnify<this>; [Unify.ignoreSymbol]?: STMUnifyIgnore; [Symbol.iterator](): Effect.EffectGenerator<STM<A, E, R>>; }
export declare namespace STM { interface Variance<out A, out E, out R> { readonly [STMTypeId]: { readonly _A: Covariant<A>; readonly _E: Covariant<E>; readonly _R: Covariant<R>; }; } }
```

#### `STM.STM.Variance`

**Replacement:** `Effect.Variance`

The distinct STM variance marker was removed with STM; use the Effect marker.

**Before**

```ts
interface Variance<out A, out E, out R> { readonly [STMTypeId]: { readonly _A: Covariant<A>; readonly _E: Covariant<E>; readonly _R: Covariant<R>; }; }
```

#### `STM.STMTypeId`

**Replacement:** `Effect.TypeId`

The distinct STM type id was removed because transactions are represented by Effect values.

**Before**

```ts
export type STMTypeId = typeof STMTypeId;
```

#### `STM.STMTypeLambda`

**Replacement:** `Effect.EffectTypeLambda`

Use the Effect type lambda; transactional requirements are represented by Effect.Transaction.

**Before**

```ts
export interface STMTypeLambda extends TypeLambda { readonly type: STM<this["Target"], this["Out1"], this["Out2"]>; }
```

#### `STM.STMUnify`

**Replacement:** `Effect.EffectUnify`

STM unification moved to ordinary Effect unification.

**Before**

```ts
export interface STMUnify<A extends { [Unify.typeSymbol]?: any; }> extends Effect.EffectUnify<A> { STM?: () => A[Unify.typeSymbol] extends STM<infer A0, infer E0, infer R0> | infer _ ? STM<A0, E0, R0> : never; }
```

#### `STM.STMUnifyIgnore`

**Replacement:** `none`

The STM-specific unification ignore marker was removed; rely on Effect inference.

**Before**

```ts

```

#### `STM.catchAll`

**Replacement:** `Effect.catch`

Use Effect.catch for typed failures. It does not catch Effect.txRetry or restore a transactional savepoint.

**Before**


**Replacement:** `Effect.catch + Option.match`

Use Effect.catch and re-fail the original error when the partial handler returns None.

**Before**

**Replacement:** `Effect.catchTag`

**Before**


**Replacement:** `Effect.suspend + Effect.txRetry`

Evaluate the predicate lazily and return Effect.void when true or Effect.txRetry when false, inside Effect.tx.

#### `STM.collect`

**Replacement:** `Effect.flatMap + Option.match + Effect.txRetry`

Map Some to success and None to Effect.txRetry inside the surrounding Effect.tx transaction.

**Before**


#### `STM.collectSTM`

**Replacement:** `Effect.flatMap + Option.match + Effect.txRetry`

Return the Effect held by Some and use Effect.txRetry for None, inside the surrounding Effect.tx transaction.

**Before**


**Replacement:** `Effect.tx`

Effect.tx runs an Effect transaction and removes its Effect.Transaction requirement.

**Before**

**Replacement:** `Effect.tx + Effect.result + Effect.fromResult`

Run Effect.tx(Effect.result(body)) before Effect.fromResult so journal changes commit even when the original transaction had a typed failure.

#### `STM.retry`

**Replacement:** `Effect.txRetry`

Do not use Effect.retry, which retries typed failures by schedule; Effect.txRetry waits for an accessed Tx value to change.

**Before**

```ts
retry: STM<never>
```

#### `STM.retryUntil`

**Replacement:** `Effect.flatMap + Effect.txRetry`

Succeed when the predicate passes; otherwise return Effect.txRetry inside Effect.tx.

**Before**

```ts

```

#### `STM.retryWhile`

**Replacement:** `Effect.flatMap + Effect.txRetry`

Return Effect.txRetry while the predicate passes; otherwise succeed inside Effect.tx.

**Before**

```ts

```

#### `STM.some`

**Replacement:** `Effect.matchEffect + Option.match`

Recreate the Option success/error shuffle explicitly; no dedicated helper remains.

**Before**

```ts

```

#### `STM.succeed`

**Replacement:** `Effect.succeed`

The combinator keeps its name, but STM values are now ordinary Effects. Run the complete transaction with Effect.tx. V4 Tx operations return ordinary Effects; compose multiple operations under one outer Effect.tx to keep them atomic.

**Before**

```ts

```

#### `STM.summarized`

**Replacement:** `Effect.gen`

Run the summary Effect before and after the body, then return the computed summary and body value.

**Before**


**Replacement:** `Effect.sync`

The combinator keeps its name, but STM values are now ordinary Effects. Run the complete transaction with Effect.tx. V4 Tx operations return ordinary Effects; compose multiple operations under one outer Effect.tx to keep them atomic.

**Before**


**Replacement:** `Effect.tap`

The combinator keeps its name, but STM values are now ordinary Effects. Run the complete transaction with Effect.tx. V4 Tx operations return ordinary Effects; compose multiple operations under one outer Effect.tx to keep them atomic.

**Before**

```ts
tap: { <A, X, E2, R2>(f: (a: A) => STM<X, E2, R2>): <E, R>(self: STM<A, E, R>) => STM<A, E2 | E, R2 | R>; <A, E, R, X, E2, R2>(self: STM<A, E, R>, f: (a: A) => STM<X, E2, R2>): STM<A, E | E2, R | R2>; }
```

**Replacement:** `Effect.tapError + Effect.tap`

Compose the separate failure and success taps.


#### `STM.tapError`

**Replacement:** `Effect.tapError`

The combinator keeps its name, but STM values are now ordinary Effects. Run the complete transaction with Effect.tx. V4 Tx operations return ordinary Effects; compose multiple operations under one outer Effect.tx to keep them atomic.

**Before**


**Replacement:** `Effect.try`

The combinator keeps its name, but STM values are now ordinary Effects. Run the complete transaction with Effect.tx. V4 Tx operations return ordinary Effects; compose multiple operations under one outer Effect.tx to keep them atomic.

**Before**


**Replacement:** `Effect.when(self, Effect.sync(() => !predicate()))`

V4 Effect.when takes an effectful condition; suspend and negate the old lazy boolean.

**Before**


**Replacement:** `Effect.when(self, Effect.map(condition, (b) => !b))`

Negate the effectful condition and use Effect.when.

**Before**

**Replacement:** `Effect.matchEffect + Option.match`

Recreate the Option error/success shuffle explicitly; no dedicated helper remains.

**Before**


#### `STM.validateAll`

**Replacement:** `Effect.validate`

The validation combinator was renamed and now returns a NonEmptyArray of errors.

**Before**

```ts

```

**Replacement:** `Effect.flip + Effect.forEach`

Flip each candidate result, traverse sequentially, then flip the aggregate to preserve all errors when every candidate fails.

**Before**

```ts

```

#### `STM.void`

**Replacement:** `Effect.void`

The combinator keeps its name, but STM values are now ordinary Effects. Run the complete transaction with Effect.tx. V4 Tx operations return ordinary Effects; compose multiple operations under one outer Effect.tx to keep them atomic.

**Before**

```ts
void_: STM<void>
```

#### `STM.when`

**Replacement:** `Effect.when(self, Effect.sync(predicate))`

V4 Effect.when takes an effectful boolean, so suspend the old lazy predicate.

**Before**

```ts
when: { (predicate: LazyArg<boolean>): <A, E, R>(self: STM<A, E, R>) => STM<Option.Option<A>, E, R>; <A, E, R>(self: STM<A, E, R>, predicate: LazyArg<boolean>): STM<Option.Option<A>, E, R>; }
```

#### `STM.whenSTM`

**Replacement:** `Effect.when`

The effectful-condition form is now the only Effect.when form.

**Before**

```ts
whenSTM: { <E2, R2>(predicate: STM<boolean, E2, R2>): <A, E, R>(self: STM<A, E, R>) => STM<Option.Option<A>, E2 | E, R2 | R>; <A, E, R, E2, R2>(self: STM<A, E, R>, predicate: STM<boolean, E2, R2>): STM<Option.Option<A>, E | E2, R | R2>; }
```

#### `STM.zipLeft`

**Replacement:** `Effect.zipWith(self, that, (left) => left)`

Use sequential Effect.zipWith and retain the left result.

**Before**

```ts
zipLeft: { <A1, E1, R1>(that: STM<A1, E1, R1>): <A, E, R>(self: STM<A, E, R>) => STM<A, E1 | E, R1 | R>; <A, E, R, A1, E1, R1>(self: STM<A, E, R>, that: STM<A1, E1, R1>): STM<A, E | E1, R | R1>; }
```

#### `STM.zipRight`

**Replacement:** `Effect.andThen`

Use Effect.andThen for sequential composition that retains the right result.

**Before**

```ts
zipRight: { <A1, E1, R1>(that: STM<A1, E1, R1>): <A, E, R>(self: STM<A, E, R>) => STM<A1, E1 | E, R1 | R>; <A, E, R, A1, E1, R1>(self: STM<A, E, R>, that: STM<A1, E1, R1>): STM<A1, E | E1, R | R1>; }
```

### `effect/Schedule`

#### `Schedule.CurrentIterationMetadata`

**Replacement:** `Schedule.CurrentMetadata`

The Context.Reference was renamed and now provides Schedule.Metadata with input, output, attempt, duration, and elapsed timing fields.

**Before**

```ts
export interface CurrentIterationMetadata { readonly _: unique symbol; }
```

- `Schedule.IterationMetadata` -> `Schedule.Metadata`: The metadata model now includes duration and uses attempt instead of recurrence; elapsed fields are millisecond numbers.

#### `Schedule.Schedule`

**Replacement:** `Schedule.Schedule`

The model remains but now has Schedule<Output, Input, Error, Env>; its public initial/step fields were replaced by Schedule.toStep and fromStep.

**Before**

```ts
export interface Schedule<out Out, in In = unknown, out R = never> extends Schedule.Variance<Out, In, R>, Pipeable { readonly initial: any; step(now: number, input: In, state: any): Effect.Effect<readonly [any, Out, ScheduleDecision.ScheduleDecision], never, R>; }
export declare namespace Schedule { interface Variance<out Out, in In, out R> { readonly [ScheduleTypeId]: { readonly _Out: Types.Covariant<Out>; readonly _In: Types.Contravariant<In>; readonly _R: Types.Covariant<R>; }; } interface DriverVariance<out Out, in In, out R> { readonly [ScheduleDriverTypeId]: { readonly _Out: Types.Covariant<Out>; readonly _In: Types.Contravariant<In>; readonly _R: Types.Covariant<R>; }; } }
```

**After**

```ts
export interface Schedule<out Output, in Input = unknown, out Error = never, out Env = never> extends Schedule.Variance<Output, Input, Error, Env>, Pipeable { }
export declare namespace Schedule { interface Variance<out Output, in Input, out Error, out Env> { readonly [TypeId]: VarianceStruct<Output, Input, Error, Env>; } interface VarianceStruct<out Output, in Input, out Error, out Env> { readonly _Out: Covariant<Output>; readonly _In: Contravariant<Input>; readonly _Error: Covariant<Error>; readonly _Env: Covariant<Env>; } }
```

#### `Schedule.Schedule.DriverVariance`

**Replacement:** `none`

ScheduleDriver was removed in v4, so its variance marker has no replacement. Use the Schedule type parameters or the function returned by Schedule.toStepWithSleep.

**Before**

```ts
interface DriverVariance<out Out, in In, out R> { readonly [ScheduleDriverTypeId]: { readonly _Out: Types.Covariant<Out>; readonly _In: Types.Contravariant<In>; readonly _R: Types.Covariant<R>; }; }
```

#### `Schedule.Schedule.Variance`

**Replacement:** `Schedule.Schedule.Variance`

The variance marker remains and now tracks Output, Input, Error, and Env through the private Schedule TypeId.

**Before**

```ts
interface Variance<out Out, in In, out R> { readonly [ScheduleTypeId]: { readonly _Out: Types.Covariant<Out>; readonly _In: Types.Contravariant<In>; readonly _R: Types.Covariant<R>; }; }
```

**After**

```ts
interface Variance<out Output, in Input, out Error, out Env> { readonly [TypeId]: VarianceStruct<Output, Input, Error, Env>; }
```

#### `Schedule.ScheduleDriver`

**Replacement:** `Schedule.toStepWithSleep`

ScheduleDriver was removed. The acquired step function provides manual next calls with automatic sleeping; Schedule.toStep exposes raw delays.

**Before**

```ts
export interface ScheduleDriver<out Out, in In = unknown, out R = never> extends Schedule.DriverVariance<Out, In, R> { readonly state: Effect.Effect<unknown>; readonly iterationMeta: Ref.Ref<IterationMetadata>; readonly last: Effect.Effect<Out, Cause.NoSuchElementException>; readonly reset: Effect.Effect<void>; next(input: In): Effect.Effect<Out, Option.Option<never>, R>; }
```

#### `Schedule.ScheduleDriverTypeId`

**Replacement:** `none`

ScheduleDriver and its public type id were removed. Use the step function returned by Schedule.toStepWithSleep.

**Before**

```ts
export type ScheduleDriverTypeId = typeof ScheduleDriverTypeId;
```

#### `Schedule.ScheduleTypeId`

**Replacement:** `none`

The Schedule type id is private in v4. Use Schedule.isSchedule to narrow unknown values.

**Before**

```ts
export type ScheduleTypeId = typeof ScheduleTypeId;
```

#### `Schedule.addDelayEffect`

**Replacement:** `Schedule.addDelay`

The v4 function is effectful by default and its callback receives full Schedule.Metadata; read metadata.output when only the prior output is needed.

**Before**

```ts
addDelayEffect: { <Out, R2>(f: (out: Out) => Effect.Effect<Duration.DurationInput, never, R2>): <In, R>(self: Schedule<Out, In, R>) => Schedule<Out, In, R2 | R>; <Out, In, R, R2>(self: Schedule<Out, In, R>, f: (out: Out) => Effect.Effect<Duration.DurationInput, never, R2>): Schedule<Out, In, R | R2>; }
```

#### `Schedule.andThenEither`

**Replacement:** `Schedule.andThenResult`

Sequential phase tagging now uses Result: self outputs are Result.fail and the following schedule outputs are Result.succeed.

**Before**

```ts

```

#### `Schedule.as`

**Replacement:** `Schedule.map`

Map the metadata to the constant output; Schedule.map accepts either a plain value or an Effect.

**Before**

```ts
as: { <Out2>(out: Out2): <Out, In, R>(self: Schedule<Out, In, R>) => Schedule<Out2, In, R>; <Out, In, R, Out2>(self: Schedule<Out, In, R>, out: Out2): Schedule<Out2, In, R>; }
```

#### `Schedule.asVoid`

**Replacement:** `Schedule.map`

Map every output to undefined.

**Before**

```ts
asVoid: <Out, In, R>(self: Schedule<Out, In, R>) => Schedule<void, In, R>
```

#### `Schedule.bothInOut`

**Replacement:** `none`

There is no direct v4 combinator preserving this output shape. Rebuild it with Schedule.fromStep and Schedule.toStep; schedule steps now return [output, Duration] and terminate with Cause.done.

**Before**

```ts
bothInOut: { <Out2, In2, R2>(that: Schedule<Out2, In2, R2>): <Out, In, R>(self: Schedule<Out, In, R>) => Schedule<[Out, Out2], readonly [In, In2], R2 | R>; <Out, In, R, Out2, In2, R2>(self: Schedule<Out, In, R>, that: Schedule<Out2, In2, R2>): Schedule<[Out, Out2], readonly [In, In2], R | R2>; }
```

#### `Schedule.check`

**Replacement:** `Schedule.while`

Continue while a predicate over metadata.input and metadata.output returns true.

**Before**

```ts
check: { <In, Out>(test: (input: In, output: Out) => boolean): <R>(self: Schedule<Out, In, R>) => Schedule<Out, In, R>; <Out, In, R>(self: Schedule<Out, In, R>, test: (input: In, output: Out) => boolean): Schedule<Out, In, R>; }
```

**Replacement:** `Schedule.while`

Schedule.while accepts an effectful metadata predicate in v4.


**Replacement:** `none`

**Replacement:** `none`

This stateful collection combinator was removed during the v4 Schedule simplification. Rebuild it with Schedule.fromStep and Schedule.toStep, keeping accumulation state inside the acquired step closure.

**Before**

**Replacement:** `none`

This stateful collection combinator was removed during the v4 Schedule simplification. Rebuild it with Schedule.fromStep and Schedule.toStep, keeping accumulation state inside the acquired step closure.

**Replacement:** `none`

This stateful collection combinator was removed during the v4 Schedule simplification. Rebuild it with Schedule.fromStep and Schedule.toStep, keeping accumulation state inside the acquired step closure.

**Replacement:** `none`

There is no direct v4 combinator preserving this output shape. Rebuild it with Schedule.fromStep and Schedule.toStep; schedule steps now return [output, Duration] and terminate with Cause.done.

#### `Scheduler.ControlledScheduler`

**Replacement:** `none`

#### `Scheduler.MixedScheduler`

**Replacement:** `Scheduler.MixedScheduler`

The class remains with a redesigned constructor and makeDispatcher-based task API.

**Before**

```ts

```

**After**

```ts

```

#### `Scheduler.PriorityBuckets`

**Replacement:** `none`

Priority buckets are now an internal Scheduler implementation detail.

**Before**

```ts

```

**Replacement:** `Scheduler.SchedulerDispatcher`


#### `Scheduler.SyncScheduler`

**Replacement:** `new Scheduler.MixedScheduler("sync")`

Use a synchronous MixedScheduler and its dispatcher; call flush when directly driving queued tasks.

**Before**


**Before**


**Replacement:** `Queue.Queue`

**Before**

```ts

```

#### `SingleProducerAsyncInput.make`

**Replacement:** `Queue.make`

Use v4 Queue producer and consumer views and bridge to Channel with Channel.fromQueue, Channel.callback, or Channel.fromPull. Queue.make({ capacity: 0 }) is the closest rendezvous backpressure but is not one-for-one.

### `effect/Sink`

#### `Sink.Sink`

**Replacement:** `Sink`

Interface kept as Sink<A, In, L, E, R> with the same type parameters; the internal representation changed from a Channel wrapper to a `transform: (upstream: Pull<NonEmptyReadonlyArray<In>>, scope) => Effect<End<A, L>>` function, and completion is the tuple `Sink.End<A, L> = readonly [value, leftover?]`.

**Before**

```ts
export interface Sink<out A, in In = unknown, out L = never, out E = never, out R = never> extends Sink.Variance<A, In, L, E, R>, Pipeable { }
export declare namespace Sink { interface Variance<out A, in In, out L, out E, out R> { readonly [SinkTypeId]: VarianceStruct<A, In, L, E, R>; } interface VarianceStruct<out A, in In, out L, out E, out R> { _A: Types.Covariant<A>; _In: Types.Contravariant<In>; _L: Types.Covariant<L>; _E: Types.Covariant<E>; _R: Types.Covariant<R>; } }
```

**After**

```ts
export interface Sink<out A, in In = unknown, out L = never, out E = never, out R = never> extends Sink.Variance<A, In, L, E, R>, Pipeable { readonly transform: (upstream: Pull.Pull<NonEmptyReadonlyArray<In>, never, void>, scope: Scope.Scope) => Effect.Effect<End<A, L>, E, R>; [Unify.typeSymbol]?: unknown; [Unify.unifySymbol]?: SinkUnify<this>; [Unify.ignoreSymbol]?: SinkUnifyIgnore; }
export declare namespace Sink { interface Variance<out A, in In, out L, out E, out R> { readonly [TypeId]: VarianceStruct<A, In, L, E, R>; } interface VarianceStruct<out A, in In, out L, out E, out R> { _A: Types.Covariant<A>; _In: Types.Contravariant<In>; _L: Types.Covariant<L>; _E: Types.Covariant<E>; _R: Types.Covariant<R>; } }
```

#### `Sink.Sink.Variance`

**Replacement:** `Sink.Variance`

Still exists as the namespace interface Sink.Variance<A, In, L, E, R> (with Sink.VarianceStruct); the variance key is now the internal string "~effect/Sink" instead of the SinkTypeId symbol.

**Before**

```ts
interface Variance<out A, in In, out L, out E, out R> { readonly [SinkTypeId]: VarianceStruct<A, In, L, E, R>; }
```

**After**

```ts
interface Variance<out A, in In, out L, out E, out R> { readonly [TypeId]: VarianceStruct<A, In, L, E, R>; }
```

#### `Sink.SinkTypeId`

**Replacement:** `none`

The type id is the unexported internal string "~effect/Sink" (no unique symbol, no export); use the new guard Sink.isSink(u) instead of checking the symbol.

**Before**

```ts
export type SinkTypeId = typeof SinkTypeId;
```

#### `Sink.SinkUnify`

**Replacement:** `SinkUnify`

Kept with the same name and shape (extends Effect.EffectUnify, preserves all five Sink type parameters).

**Before**

```ts
export interface SinkUnify<A extends { [Unify.typeSymbol]?: any; }> extends Effect.EffectUnify<A> { Sink?: () => A[Unify.typeSymbol] extends Sink<infer A, infer In, infer L, infer E, infer R> | infer _ ? Sink<A, In, L, E, R> : never; }
```

**After**

```ts
export interface SinkUnify<A extends { [Unify.typeSymbol]?: any; }> extends Effect.EffectUnify<A> { Sink?: () => A[Unify.typeSymbol] extends Sink<infer A, infer In, infer L, infer E, infer R> | infer _ ? Sink<A, In, L, E, R> : never; }
```

#### `Sink.SinkUnifyIgnore`

**Replacement:** `SinkUnifyIgnore`

Kept with the same name; now a standalone `{ Effect?: true }` interface instead of extending Effect.EffectUnifyIgnore.

**Before**

```ts

```

**After**

```ts
export interface SinkUnifyIgnore { Effect?: true; }
```

- `Sink.collectAll` -> `Sink.collect`: Renamed; returns Sink<Array<In>, In> collecting into a plain mutable Array instead of Chunk.

#### `Sink.collectAllFrom`

**Replacement:** `none`

Repeated-run result accumulation was removed; checked the v4 export list (no collectAllFrom/repeatedly). Re-implement with Sink.fromTransform, looping self.transform on the upstream pull (feeding leftovers back) until the upstream ends, accumulating results in an array.

**Before**

```ts
collectAllFrom: <A, In, L extends In, E, R>(self: Sink<A, In, L, E, R>) => Sink<Chunk.Chunk<A>, In, L, E, R>
```

- `Sink.collectAllN` -> `Sink.take`: Sink.take(n) returns Sink<Array<In>, In, In> collecting up to n elements (Array instead of Chunk), emitting the unconsumed remainder as leftovers.

#### `Sink.collectAllToMap`

**Replacement:** `Sink.reduce`

Built-in HashMap collector removed; build a plain Map in the reducer: Sink.reduce(() => new Map<K, In>(), (m, in_) => { const k = key(in_); return m.set(k, m.has(k) ? merge(m.get(k)!, in_) : in_) }).

**Before**

```ts
collectAllToMap: <In, K>(key: (input: In) => K, merge: (x: In, y: In) => In) => Sink<HashMap.HashMap<K, In>, In>
```

#### `Sink.collectAllToMapN`

**Replacement:** `none`

Removed; approximating with Sink.reduceWhile((...) , (m) => m.size < n, ...) consumes (merges) the element that introduces the (n+1)-th key, whereas v3 left it as leftover — exact v3 leftover behavior needs a custom Sink.fromTransform that checks the key before consuming.

**Before**

```ts
collectAllToMapN: <In, K>(n: number, key: (input: In) => K, merge: (x: In, y: In) => In) => Sink<HashMap.HashMap<K, In>, In, In>
```

#### `Sink.collectAllToSet`

**Replacement:** `Sink.reduce`

Built-in HashSet collector removed; build a plain Set: Sink.reduce(() => new Set<In>(), (s, in_) => s.add(in_)).

**Before**

```ts
collectAllToSet: <In>() => Sink<HashSet.HashSet<In>, In>
```

- `Sink.collectAllToSetN` -> `Sink.reduceWhile`: Removed; equivalent via Sink.reduceWhile(() => new Set<In>(), (s) => s.size < n, (s, in_) => s.add(in_)) — stops with leftovers once n distinct values are collected (plain Set instead of HashSet).

#### `Sink.collectAllUntil`

**Replacement:** `Sink.takeUntil`

Renamed; Sink.takeUntil(predicate) collects into Array<In> until the predicate matches, including the matching element, like v3.

**Before**

```ts
collectAllUntil: <In>(p: Predicate<In>) => Sink<Chunk.Chunk<In>, In, In>
```

#### `Sink.collectAllUntilEffect`

**Replacement:** `Sink.takeUntilEffect`

Renamed; Sink.takeUntilEffect(p) collects into Array<In> until the effectful predicate returns true, including the matching element.

**Before**

```ts
collectAllUntilEffect: <In, E, R>(p: (input: In) => Effect.Effect<boolean, E, R>) => Sink<Chunk.Chunk<In>, In, In, E, R>
```

#### `Sink.collectAllWhile`

**Replacement:** `Sink.takeWhile`

Renamed; Sink.takeWhile(predicate) collects the matching prefix into Array<In>, keeps the refinement overload, and excludes the first failing element (returned via leftovers).

**Before**

```ts
collectAllWhile: { <In, Out extends In>(refinement: Refinement<In, Out>): Sink<Chunk.Chunk<Out>, In, In>; <In>(predicate: Predicate<In>): Sink<Chunk.Chunk<In>, In, In>; }
```

#### `Sink.collectAllWhileEffect`

**Replacement:** `Sink.takeWhileEffect`

Renamed; Sink.takeWhileEffect(p) collects into Array<In> while the effectful predicate returns true.

**Before**

```ts
collectAllWhileEffect: <In, E, R>(predicate: (input: In) => Effect.Effect<boolean, E, R>) => Sink<Chunk.Chunk<In>, In, In, E, R>
```

#### `Sink.collectAllWhileWith`

**Replacement:** `none`

Repeatedly-run-and-fold was removed (no v4 counterpart in the export list); re-implement with Sink.fromTransform looping self.transform while the `while` predicate holds on each result, folding results with `body` and feeding leftovers back into the next run.

**Before**

```ts
collectAllWhileWith: { <A, S>(options: { readonly initial: S; readonly while: Predicate<A>; readonly body: (s: S, a: A) => S; }): <In, L extends In, E, R>(self: Sink<A, In, L, E, R>) => Sink<S, In, L, E, R>; <A, In, L extends In, E, R, S>(self: Sink<A, In, L, E, R>, options: { readonly initial: S; readonly while: Predicate<A>; readonly body: (s: S, a: A) => S; }): Sink<S, In, L, E, R>; }
```

#### `Sink.collectLeftover`

**Replacement:** `Sink.mapEnd`

Use Sink.mapEnd to move the leftovers into the result: Sink.mapEnd(self, ([a, leftover]) => [[a, leftover ?? []] as const]); leftovers are NonEmptyReadonlyArray<L> | undefined instead of Chunk<L>.

**Before**

```ts
collectLeftover: <A, In, L, E, R>(self: Sink<A, In, L, E, R>) => Sink<[A, Chunk.Chunk<L>], In, never, E, R>
```

- `Sink.context` -> `Sink.fromEffect(Effect.context())`: Sink.context was removed; Sink.fromEffect(Effect.context<R>()) yields the same Sink<Context<R>, unknown, never, never, R>.

**Replacement:** `Sink.fromEffect(Effect.contextWith(f))`

Removed; compose Sink.fromEffect with Effect.contextWith to derive a value from the context.

**Replacement:** `Sink.fromEffect(Effect.flatMap(Effect.context(), f))`

Removed, and v4 Effect has no contextWithEffect; use Sink.fromEffect(Effect.flatMap(Effect.context<R0>(), f)).

**Before**

#### `Sink.contextWithSink`

**Replacement:** `Sink.unwrap(Effect.contextWith(f))`

Removed; Sink.unwrap(Effect.contextWith((ctx: Context.Context<R0>) => f(ctx))) builds the sink from the context.

**Before**

```ts
contextWithSink: <R0, A, In, L, E, R>(f: (context: Context.Context<R0>) => Sink<A, In, L, E, R>) => Sink<A, In, L, E, R0 | R>
```

#### `Sink.dieMessage`

**Replacement:** `Sink.die`

Removed (v4 has no RuntimeException-based dieMessage anywhere); use Sink.die(new Error(message)).

**Before**

```ts
dieMessage: (message: string) => Sink<never, unknown>
```

#### `Sink.dieSync`

**Replacement:** `Sink.failCauseSync`

Removed; use Sink.failCauseSync(() => Cause.die(evaluate())) to defer defect evaluation, or Sink.die(defect) when eager is fine.

**Before**

```ts
dieSync: (evaluate: LazyArg<unknown>) => Sink<never, unknown>
```

#### `Sink.dimap`

**Replacement:** `Sink.mapInput + Sink.map`

Removed; compose the two halves: self.pipe(Sink.mapInput(f), Sink.map(g)).

**Before**

```ts
dimap: { <In0, In, A, A2>(options: { readonly onInput: (input: In0) => In; readonly onDone: (a: A) => A2; }): <L, E, R>(self: Sink<A, In, L, E, R>) => Sink<A2, In0, L, E, R>; <A, In, L, E, R, In0, A2>(self: Sink<A, In, L, E, R>, options: { readonly onInput: (input: In0) => In; readonly onDone: (a: A) => A2; }): Sink<A2, In0, L, E, R>; }
```

#### `Sink.dimapChunks`

**Replacement:** `Sink.mapInputArray + Sink.map`

Removed; compose self.pipe(Sink.mapInputArray(f), Sink.map(g)) — f now maps NonEmptyReadonlyArray instead of Chunk and must return a non-empty array.

**Before**

```ts
dimapChunks: { <In0, In, A, A2>(options: { readonly onInput: (chunk: Chunk.Chunk<In0>) => Chunk.Chunk<In>; readonly onDone: (a: A) => A2; }): <L, E, R>(self: Sink<A, In, L, E, R>) => Sink<A2, In0, L, E, R>; <A, In, L, E, R, In0, A2>(self: Sink<A, In, L, E, R>, options: { readonly onInput: (chunk: Chunk.Chunk<In0>) => Chunk.Chunk<In>; readonly onDone: (a: A) => A2; }): Sink<A2, In0, L, E, R>; }
```

#### `Sink.dimapChunksEffect`

**Replacement:** `Sink.mapInputArrayEffect + Sink.mapEffect`

Removed; compose self.pipe(Sink.mapInputArrayEffect(f), Sink.mapEffect(g)) — f maps NonEmptyReadonlyArray instead of Chunk and must return a non-empty array.

**Before**

```ts
dimapChunksEffect: { <In0, In, E2, R2, A, A2, E3, R3>(options: { readonly onInput: (chunk: Chunk.Chunk<In0>) => Effect.Effect<Chunk.Chunk<In>, E2, R2>; readonly onDone: (a: A) => Effect.Effect<A2, E3, R3>; }): <L, E, R>(self: Sink<A, In, L, E, R>) => Sink<A2, In0, L, E2 | E3 | E, R2 | R3 | R>; <A, In, L, E, R, In0, E2, R2, A2, E3, R3>(self: Sink<A, In, L, E, R>, options: { readonly onInput: (chunk: Chunk.Chunk<In0>) => Effect.Effect<Chunk.Chunk<In>, E2, R2>; readonly onDone: (a: A) => Effect.Effect<A2, E3, R3>; }): Sink<A2, In0, L, E | E2 | E3, R | R2 | R3>; }
```

#### `Sink.dimapEffect`

**Replacement:** `Sink.mapInputEffect + Sink.mapEffect`

Removed; compose self.pipe(Sink.mapInputEffect(f), Sink.mapEffect(g)).

**Before**

```ts
dimapEffect: { <In0, In, E2, R2, A, A2, E3, R3>(options: { readonly onInput: (input: In0) => Effect.Effect<In, E2, R2>; readonly onDone: (a: A) => Effect.Effect<A2, E3, R3>; }): <L, E, R>(self: Sink<A, In, L, E, R>) => Sink<A2, In0, L, E2 | E3 | E, R2 | R3 | R>; <A, In, L, E, R, In0, E2, R2, A2, E3, R3>(self: Sink<A, In, L, E, R>, options: { readonly onInput: (input: In0) => Effect.Effect<In, E2, R2>; readonly onDone: (a: A) => Effect.Effect<A2, E3, R3>; }): Sink<A2, In0, L, E | E2 | E3, R | R2 | R3>; }
```

#### `Sink.drop`

**Replacement:** `none`

The drop* sinks were removed (nothing in the v4 export list); drop on the stream side instead with Stream.drop(n) before running the sink, or write a Sink.fromTransform that discards the first n pulled elements.

**Before**

```ts
drop: <In>(n: number) => Sink<unknown, In, In>
```

#### `Sink.dropUntil`

**Replacement:** `none`

Removed with the other drop* sinks; use Stream.dropUntil(predicate) on the stream before running the sink.

**Before**

```ts
dropUntil: <In>(predicate: Predicate<In>) => Sink<unknown, In, In>
```

- `Sink.dropUntilEffect` -> `none`: Removed; use Stream.dropUntilEffect(p) on the stream before running the sink.

#### `Sink.dropWhile`

**Replacement:** `none`

Removed; use Stream.dropWhile(predicate) on the stream before running the sink.

**Before**

```ts
dropWhile: <In>(predicate: Predicate<In>) => Sink<unknown, In, In>
```

#### `Sink.dropWhileEffect`

**Replacement:** `none`

Removed; use Stream.dropWhileEffect(p) on the stream before running the sink.

**Before**

```ts
dropWhileEffect: <In, E, R>(predicate: (input: In) => Effect.Effect<boolean, E, R>) => Sink<unknown, In, In, E, R>
```

#### `Sink.ensuringWith`

**Replacement:** `Sink.onExit`

Renamed; Sink.onExit(self, (exit: Exit<A, E>) => finalizer) runs after completion, failure, or interruption — the exit now carries the sink's result value A (v3 passed Exit<unknown, E>). Plain Sink.ensuring(effect) also still exists for the exit-independent case.

**Before**

```ts
ensuringWith: { <A, E, X, R2>(finalizer: (exit: Exit.Exit<A, E>) => Effect.Effect<X, never, R2>): <In, L, R>(self: Sink<A, In, L, E, R>) => Sink<A, In, L, E, R2 | R>; <A, In, L, E, R, X, R2>(self: Sink<A, In, L, E, R>, finalizer: (exit: Exit.Exit<A, E>) => Effect.Effect<X, never, R2>): Sink<A, In, L, E, R | R2>; }
```

#### `Sink.filterInput`

**Replacement:** `none`

Removed, and not expressible via Sink.mapInputArray because its function must return a non-empty array (a fully-filtered batch is illegal); filter on the stream with Stream.filter(predicate) before running the sink, or write a Sink.fromTransform that skips empty filtered batches.

**Before**

```ts
filterInput: { <In, In1 extends In, In2 extends In1>(f: Refinement<In1, In2>): <A, L, E, R>(self: Sink<A, In, L, E, R>) => Sink<A, In2, L, E, R>; <In, In1 extends In>(f: Predicate<In1>): <A, L, E, R>(self: Sink<A, In, L, E, R>) => Sink<A, In1, L, E, R>; }
```

#### `Sink.filterInputEffect`

**Replacement:** `none`

Removed (same non-empty-array constraint as filterInput); use Stream.filterEffect(p) on the stream before running the sink.

**Before**

```ts
filterInputEffect: { <In, In1 extends In, E2, R2>(f: (input: In1) => Effect.Effect<boolean, E2, R2>): <A, L, E, R>(self: Sink<A, In, L, E, R>) => Sink<A, In1, L, E2 | E, R2 | R>; <A, In, L, E, R, In1 extends In, E2, R2>(self: Sink<A, In, L, E, R>, f: (input: In1) => Effect.Effect<boolean, E2, R2>): Sink<A, In1, L, E | E2, R | R2>; }
```

#### `Sink.foldChunks`

**Replacement:** `Sink.reduceWhileArray`

Sink.reduceWhileArray(() => s, contFn, f) folds whole input batches; initial state is now a lazy thunk and f receives NonEmptyReadonlyArray<In> instead of Chunk<In>.

**Before**

```ts
foldChunks: <S, In>(s: S, contFn: Predicate<S>, f: (s: S, chunk: Chunk.Chunk<In>) => S) => Sink<S, In>
```

#### `Sink.foldChunksEffect`

**Replacement:** `Sink.reduceWhileArrayEffect`

Sink.reduceWhileArrayEffect(() => s, contFn, f) is the effectful array-level fold with continuation predicate; lazy initial state, NonEmptyReadonlyArray instead of Chunk. Sink.foldArray has the same shape but does not check contFn on the initial state.

**Before**

```ts
foldChunksEffect: <S, In, E, R>(s: S, contFn: Predicate<S>, f: (s: S, chunk: Chunk.Chunk<In>) => Effect.Effect<S, E, R>) => Sink<S, In, In, E, R>
```

#### `Sink.foldEffect`

**Replacement:** `Sink.reduceWhileEffect`

Sink.reduceWhileEffect(() => s, contFn, f) folds element-by-element with an effectful step and continuation predicate (checked on the initial state, like v3); initial state is now a lazy thunk. v4 Sink.fold has the same signature but skips the initial-state check.

**Before**

```ts
foldEffect: <S, In, E, R>(s: S, contFn: Predicate<S>, f: (s: S, input: In) => Effect.Effect<S, E, R>) => Sink<S, In, In, E, R>
```

- `Sink.foldLeft` -> `Sink.reduce`: Renamed; Sink.reduce(() => s, f) — initial state is now a lazy thunk, semantics otherwise identical.

#### `Sink.foldLeftChunks`

**Replacement:** `Sink.reduceArray`

Renamed; Sink.reduceArray(() => s, f) folds whole batches — lazy initial state, f receives NonEmptyReadonlyArray<In> instead of Chunk<In>.

**Before**

```ts
foldLeftChunks: <S, In>(s: S, f: (s: S, chunk: Chunk.Chunk<In>) => S) => Sink<S, In>
```

#### `Sink.foldLeftChunksEffect`

**Replacement:** `Sink.reduceWhileArrayEffect`

No plain reduceArrayEffect exists in v4; use Sink.reduceWhileArrayEffect(() => s, () => true, f) (constant-true predicate) — f receives NonEmptyReadonlyArray<In> instead of Chunk<In> and the result has L = never like v3.

**Before**

```ts
foldLeftChunksEffect: <S, In, E, R>(s: S, f: (s: S, chunk: Chunk.Chunk<In>) => Effect.Effect<S, E, R>) => Sink<S, In, never, E, R>
```

#### `Sink.foldLeftEffect`

**Replacement:** `Sink.reduceEffect`

Renamed; Sink.reduceEffect(() => s, f) — lazy initial state, effectful step, no termination predicate.

**Before**

```ts
foldLeftEffect: <S, In, E, R>(s: S, f: (s: S, input: In) => Effect.Effect<S, E, R>) => Sink<S, In, In, E, R>
```

#### `Sink.foldSink`

**Replacement:** `Sink.orElse + Sink.flatMap`

The two-channel match was removed; compose self.pipe(Sink.orElse((e) => options.onFailure(e)), Sink.flatMap((a) => options.onSuccess(a))) — orElse switches to the failure sink (resuming the same upstream), flatMap feeds leftovers to the success sink first.

**Before**

```ts
foldSink: { <E, A1, In, In1 extends In, L1, E1, R1, A, A2, In2 extends In, L2, E2, R2>(options: { readonly onFailure: (err: E) => Sink<A1, In1, L1, E1, R1>; readonly onSuccess: (a: A) => Sink<A2, In2, L2, E2, R2>; }): <L, R>(self: Sink<A, In, L, E, R>) => Sink<A1 | A2, In1 & In2, L1 | L2, E1 | E2, R1 | R2 | R>; <A, In, L, E, R, A1, In1 extends In, L1, E1, R1, A2, In2 extends In, L2, E2, R2>(self: Sink<A, In, L, E, R>, options: { readonly onFailure: (err: E) => Sink<A1, In1, L1, E1, R1>; readonly onSuccess: (a: A) => Sink<A2, In2, L2, E2, R2>; }): Sink<A1 | A2, In1 & In2, L1 | L2, E1 | E2, R | R1 | R2>; }
```

- `Sink.foldUntilEffect` -> `Sink.foldUntil`: v4 Sink.foldUntil(() => s, max, f) takes the effectful step function directly (f returns Effect<S, E, R>), so it covers v3 foldUntilEffect; initial state is now a lazy thunk. For the pure v3 foldUntil wrap the step in Effect.succeed.

#### `Sink.foldWeighted`

**Replacement:** `none`

The whole foldWeighted family was removed from v4 Sink (checked the export list); re-implement with Sink.fold carrying the accumulated cost in the state (cont while cost < max), returning leftovers automatically when stopping mid-batch.

**Before**

```ts
foldWeighted: <S, In>(options: { readonly initial: S; readonly maxCost: number; readonly cost: (s: S, input: In) => number; readonly body: (s: S, input: In) => S; }) => Sink<S, In, In>
```

#### `Sink.foldWeightedDecompose`

**Replacement:** `none`

Removed with no decompose mechanism in v4; splitting oversized elements must happen upstream (transform the stream before the sink) or inside a custom Sink.fromTransform.

**Before**

```ts
foldWeightedDecompose: <S, In>(options: { readonly initial: S; readonly maxCost: number; readonly cost: (s: S, input: In) => number; readonly decompose: (input: In) => Chunk.Chunk<In>; readonly body: (s: S, input: In) => S; }) => Sink<S, In, In>
```

#### `Sink.foldWeightedDecomposeEffect`

**Replacement:** `none`

Removed; same as foldWeightedDecompose — no effectful weighted/decompose fold exists, re-implement via Sink.fromTransform or restructure upstream.

**Before**

```ts
foldWeightedDecomposeEffect: <S, In, E, R, E2, R2, E3, R3>(options: { readonly initial: S; readonly maxCost: number; readonly cost: (s: S, input: In) => Effect.Effect<number, E, R>; readonly decompose: (input: In) => Effect.Effect<Chunk.Chunk<In>, E2, R2>; readonly body: (s: S, input: In) => Effect.Effect<S, E3, R3>; }) => Sink<S, In, In, E | E2 | E3, R | R2 | R3>
```

#### `Sink.foldWeightedEffect`

**Replacement:** `none`

Removed; re-implement with Sink.fold (its step is effectful in v4) tracking accumulated cost in the state.

**Before**

```ts
foldWeightedEffect: <S, In, E, R, E2, R2>(options: { readonly initial: S; readonly maxCost: number; readonly cost: (s: S, input: In) => Effect.Effect<number, E, R>; readonly body: (s: S, input: In) => Effect.Effect<S, E2, R2>; }) => Sink<S, In, In, E | E2, R | R2>
```

#### `Sink.forEachChunk`

**Replacement:** `Sink.forEachArray`

Renamed; f receives NonEmptyReadonlyArray<In> instead of Chunk<In>.

**Before**

```ts
forEachChunk: <In, X, E, R>(f: (input: Chunk.Chunk<In>) => Effect.Effect<X, E, R>) => Sink<void, In, never, E, R>
```

#### `Sink.forEachChunkWhile`

**Replacement:** `Sink.forEachWhileArray`

Renamed; f: (NonEmptyReadonlyArray<In>) => Effect<boolean> continues while true, stops on false, as in v3.

**Before**

```ts
forEachChunkWhile: <In, E, R>(f: (input: Chunk.Chunk<In>) => Effect.Effect<boolean, E, R>) => Sink<void, In, In, E, R>
```

#### `Sink.fromPush`

**Replacement:** `Sink.fromTransform`

The push-based protocol (Option<Chunk> push function failing with [Either, leftovers]) is gone; v4's low-level constructor is pull-based: Sink.fromTransform((upstream: Pull<NonEmptyReadonlyArray<In>>, scope) => Effect<End<A, L>>) — pull inputs from upstream and finish by succeeding with the [value, leftover?] tuple.

**Before**

```ts
fromPush: <In, L0, R0, L, R>(push: Effect.Effect<(_: Option.Option<Chunk.Chunk<In>>) => Effect.Effect<void, readonly [Either.Either<R0, L0>, Chunk.Chunk<L>], R>, never, R>) => Sink<R0, In, L, L0, Exclude<R, Scope.Scope>>
```

#### `Sink.leftover`

**Replacement:** `Sink.succeed`

Removed as a standalone constructor; Sink.succeed now takes optional leftovers: Sink.succeed(void 0, leftovers) where leftovers is a NonEmptyReadonlyArray<L> instead of Chunk<L>.

**Before**

```ts
leftover: <L>(chunk: Chunk.Chunk<L>) => Sink<void, unknown, L>
```

#### `Sink.mapInputChunks`

**Replacement:** `Sink.mapInputArray`

Renamed; f maps NonEmptyReadonlyArray<In0> => NonEmptyReadonlyArray<In> (must stay non-empty) instead of Chunk => Chunk.

**Before**

```ts
mapInputChunks: { <In0, In>(f: (chunk: Chunk.Chunk<In0>) => Chunk.Chunk<In>): <A, L, E, R>(self: Sink<A, In, L, E, R>) => Sink<A, In0, L, E, R>; <A, In, L, E, R, In0>(self: Sink<A, In, L, E, R>, f: (chunk: Chunk.Chunk<In0>) => Chunk.Chunk<In>): Sink<A, In0, L, E, R>; }
```

- `Sink.mapInputChunksEffect` -> `Sink.mapInputArrayEffect`: Renamed; f maps NonEmptyReadonlyArray<In0> => Effect<NonEmptyReadonlyArray<In>> (must stay non-empty) instead of Chunk => Effect<Chunk>.

#### `Sink.mkString`

**Replacement:** `Sink.reduceArray`

Removed as a built-in; equivalent one-liner: Sink.reduceArray(() => "", (s, arr) => s + arr.join("")).

**Before**

```ts
mkString: Sink<string, unknown>
```

#### `Sink.race`

**Replacement:** `none`

Sink racing (race/raceBoth/raceWith) was removed from v4; broadcast the stream (Stream.broadcast) into two consumers and race the resulting run effects with Effect.race, or write a custom Channel.

**Before**

```ts
race: { <R1, E1, In1, L1, A1>(that: Sink<A1, In1, L1, E1, R1>): <A, In, L, E, R>(self: Sink<A, In, L, E, R>) => Sink<A1 | A, In & In1, L1 | L, E1 | E, R1 | R>; <A, In, L, E, R, A1, In1, L1, E1, R1>(self: Sink<A, In, L, E, R>, that: Sink<A1, In1, L1, E1, R1>): Sink<A | A1, In & In1, L | L1, E | E1, R | R1>; }
```

#### `Sink.raceBoth`

**Replacement:** `none`

Removed with the race family; broadcast the stream and use Effect.raceBoth (or Effect.race) on the two Stream.run effects to learn which side won.

**Before**

```ts
raceBoth: { <A1, In1, L1, E1, R1>(that: Sink<A1, In1, L1, E1, R1>, options?: { readonly capacity?: number | undefined; } | undefined): <A, In, L, E, R>(self: Sink<A, In, L, E, R>) => Sink<Either.Either<A1, A>, In & In1, L1 | L, E1 | E, R1 | R>; <A, In, L, E, R, A1, In1, L1, E1, R1>(self: Sink<A, In, L, E, R>, that: Sink<A1, In1, L1, E1, R1>, options?: { readonly capacity?: number | undefined; } | undefined): Sink<Either.Either<A1, A>, In & In1, L | L1, E | E1, R | R1>; }
```

#### `Sink.raceWith`

**Replacement:** `none`

Removed, along with the MergeDecision type it depended on; the closest is broadcasting the stream and combining the two run effects manually (Effect.raceWith on the run effects).

**Before**

```ts
raceWith: { <A2, In2, L2, E2, R2, A, E, A3, A4>(options: { readonly other: Sink<A2, In2, L2, E2, R2>; readonly onSelfDone: (exit: Exit.Exit<A, E>) => MergeDecision.MergeDecision<R2, E2, A2, E2 | E, A3>; readonly onOtherDone: (exit: Exit.Exit<A2, E2>) => MergeDecision.MergeDecision<R2, E, A, E2 | E, A4>; readonly capacity?: number | undefined; }): <In, L, R>(self: Sink<A, In, L, E, R>) => Sink<A3 | A4, In & In2, L2 | L, E2 | E, R2 | R>; <A, In, L, E, R, A2, In2, L2, E2, R2, A3, A4>(self: Sink<A, In, L, E, R>, options: { readonly other: Sink<A2, In2, L2, E2, R2>; readonly onSelfDone: (exit: Exit.Exit<A, E>) => MergeDecision.MergeDecision<R2, E2, A2, E | E2, A3>; readonly onOtherDone: (exit: Exit.Exit<A2, E2>) => MergeDecision.MergeDecision<R2, E, A, E | E2, A4>; readonly capacity?: number | undefined; }): Sink<A3 | A4, In & In2, L | L2, E | E2, R | R2>; }
```

#### `Sink.refineOrDie`

**Replacement:** `Sink.catch`

Removed; rebuild with the typed-error handler: Sink.catch(self, (e) => Option.match(pf(e), { onSome: Effect.fail, onNone: () => Effect.die(e) })) — note Sink.catch replaces the result on recovery, so refined errors must be re-failed as shown.

**Before**

```ts
refineOrDie: { <E, E2>(pf: (error: E) => Option.Option<E2>): <A, In, L, R>(self: Sink<A, In, L, E, R>) => Sink<A, In, L, E2, R>; <A, In, L, E, R, E2>(self: Sink<A, In, L, E, R>, pf: (error: E) => Option.Option<E2>): Sink<A, In, L, E2, R>; }
```

#### `Sink.refineOrDieWith`

**Replacement:** `Sink.catch`

Removed; same pattern as refineOrDie but die with the mapped defect: Sink.catch(self, (e) => Option.match(pf(e), { onSome: Effect.fail, onNone: () => Effect.die(f(e)) })).

**Before**

```ts
refineOrDieWith: { <E, E2>(pf: (error: E) => Option.Option<E2>, f: (error: E) => unknown): <A, In, L, R>(self: Sink<A, In, L, E, R>) => Sink<A, In, L, E2, R>; <A, In, L, E, R, E2>(self: Sink<A, In, L, E, R>, pf: (error: E) => Option.Option<E2>, f: (error: E) => unknown): Sink<A, In, L, E2, R>; }
```

#### `Sink.splitWhere`

**Replacement:** `none`

Removed; it re-chunked input so the sink stopped before the first later element matching the predicate — closest v4 options are pre-splitting the stream (Stream.split / Stream.takeWhile) or a custom Sink.fromTransform that cuts pulled arrays at the predicate boundary and returns the rest as leftovers.

**Before**

```ts
splitWhere: { <In>(f: Predicate<In>): <A, L extends In, E, R>(self: Sink<A, In, L, E, R>) => Sink<A, In, In, E, R>; <A, In, L extends In, E, R>(self: Sink<A, In, L, E, R>, f: Predicate<In>): Sink<A, In, In, E, R>; }
```

#### `Sink.unwrapScoped`

**Replacement:** `Sink.unwrap`

Folded into Sink.unwrap, whose signature now excludes Scope from R (Sink<..., Exclude<R, Scope> | R2>), so scoped effects are accepted directly; resources stay open for the sink's lifetime.

**Before**

```ts
unwrapScoped: <A, In, L, E, R>(effect: Effect.Effect<Sink<A, In, L, E, R>, E, R>) => Sink<A, In, L, E, Exclude<R, Scope.Scope>>
```

#### `Sink.unwrapScopedWith`

**Replacement:** `Sink.unwrap`

Folded into Sink.unwrap — obtain the scope inside the effect via Effect.scope (Sink.unwrap(Effect.flatMap(Effect.scope, f))); for direct scope access use Sink.fromTransform, whose transform receives (upstream, scope).

**Before**

```ts
unwrapScopedWith: <A, In, L, E, R>(f: (scope: Scope.Scope) => Effect.Effect<Sink<A, In, L, E, R>, E, R>) => Sink<A, In, L, E, R>
```

#### `Sink.zip`

**Replacement:** `Sink.flatMap`

The zip family was removed; sequential zip is self.pipe(Sink.flatMap((a) => Sink.map(that, (a2) => [a, a2] as const))) — leftovers of the first sink feed the second. The { concurrent: true } racing mode has no v4 equivalent.

**Before**

```ts
zip: { <A2, In, In2 extends In, L2, E2, R2>(that: Sink<A2, In2, L2, E2, R2>, options?: { readonly concurrent?: boolean | undefined; } | undefined): <A, L, E, R>(self: Sink<A, In, L, E, R>) => Sink<[A, A2], In & In2, L2 | L, E2 | E, R2 | R>; <A, In, L, E, R, A2, In2 extends In, L2, E2, R2>(self: Sink<A, In, L, E, R>, that: Sink<A2, In2, L2, E2, R2>, options?: { readonly concurrent?: boolean | undefined; } | undefined): Sink<[A, A2], In & In2, L | L2, E | E2, R | R2>; }
```

#### `Sink.zipLeft`

**Replacement:** `Sink.flatMap`

Removed; use self.pipe(Sink.flatMap((a) => Sink.as(that, a))) to run both sequentially and keep the first result (no concurrent option).

**Before**

```ts
zipLeft: { <A2, In, In2 extends In, L2, E2, R2>(that: Sink<A2, In2, L2, E2, R2>, options?: { readonly concurrent?: boolean | undefined; } | undefined): <A, L, E, R>(self: Sink<A, In, L, E, R>) => Sink<A, In & In2, L2 | L, E2 | E, R2 | R>; <A, In, L, E, R, A2, In2 extends In, L2, E2, R2>(self: Sink<A, In, L, E, R>, that: Sink<A2, In2, L2, E2, R2>, options?: { readonly concurrent?: boolean | undefined; } | undefined): Sink<A, In & In2, L | L2, E | E2, R | R2>; }
```

#### `Sink.zipRight`

**Replacement:** `Sink.flatMap`

Removed; use self.pipe(Sink.flatMap(() => that)) to run both sequentially and keep the second result (no concurrent option).

**Before**

```ts
zipRight: { <A2, In, In2 extends In, L2, E2, R2>(that: Sink<A2, In2, L2, E2, R2>, options?: { readonly concurrent?: boolean | undefined; } | undefined): <A, L, E, R>(self: Sink<A, In, L, E, R>) => Sink<A2, In & In2, L2 | L, E2 | E, R2 | R>; <A, In, L, E, R, A2, In2 extends In, L2, E2, R2>(self: Sink<A, In, L, E, R>, that: Sink<A2, In2, L2, E2, R2>, options?: { readonly concurrent?: boolean | undefined; } | undefined): Sink<A2, In & In2, L | L2, E | E2, R | R2>; }
```

#### `Sink.zipWith`

**Replacement:** `Sink.flatMap`

Removed; use self.pipe(Sink.flatMap((a) => Sink.map(that, (a2) => f(a, a2)))) — sequential only, the { concurrent: true } option has no v4 equivalent.

**Before**

```ts
zipWith: { <A2, In, In2 extends In, L2, E2, R2, A, A3>(that: Sink<A2, In2, L2, E2, R2>, f: (a: A, a2: A2) => A3, options?: { readonly concurrent?: boolean | undefined; } | undefined): <L, E, R>(self: Sink<A, In, L, E, R>) => Sink<A3, In & In2, L2 | L, E2 | E, R2 | R>; <A, In, L, E, R, A2, In2 extends In, L2, E2, R2, A3>(self: Sink<A, In, L, E, R>, that: Sink<A2, In2, L2, E2, R2>, f: (a: A, a2: A2) => A3, options?: { readonly concurrent?: boolean | undefined; } | undefined): Sink<A3, In & In2, L | L2, E | E2, R | R2>; }
```

### `effect/SortedMap`

#### `SortedMap.SortedMap`

**Replacement:** `HashMap.HashMap`

Use HashMap as the immutable core model and retain Order externally; ordered iteration and range seeks require sorting on observation.

**Before**

```ts
export interface SortedMap<in out K, out V> extends Iterable<[K, V]>, Equal.Equal, Pipeable, Inspectable { readonly [TypeId]: { readonly _K: Types.Invariant<K>; readonly _V: Types.Covariant<V>; }; }
```

#### `SortedMap.TypeId`

**Replacement:** `none`

The SortedMap brand was removed and HashMap.TypeId is private; use HashMap.isHashMap when a guard is needed.

**Before**

```ts
export type TypeId = typeof TypeId;
```

#### `SortedMap.empty`

**Replacement:** `HashMap.empty`

SortedMap was removed; use an immutable HashMap and retain the key Order separately.

**Before**

```ts
empty: <K, V = never>(ord: Order<K>) => SortedMap<K, V>
```

#### `SortedMap.entries`

**Replacement:** `HashMap.entries + Array.sortWith`

Materialize HashMap.entries and sort by key with the retained Order when ordered traversal is required.

**Before**

```ts
entries: <K, V>(self: SortedMap<K, V>) => IterableIterator<[K, V]>
```

#### `SortedMap.fromIterable`

**Replacement:** `HashMap.fromIterable`

Use HashMap.fromIterable and retain the key Order separately; duplicate keys collapse.

**Before**

```ts
fromIterable: { <B>(ord: Order<B>): <K extends B, V>(iterable: Iterable<readonly [K, V]>) => SortedMap<K, V>; <K extends B, V, B>(iterable: Iterable<readonly [K, V]>, ord: Order<B>): SortedMap<K, V>; }
```

#### `SortedMap.get`

**Replacement:** `HashMap.get`

Direct optional lookup on the replacement immutable map.

**Before**

```ts
get: { <K>(key: K): <V>(self: SortedMap<K, V>) => Option.Option<V>; <K, V>(self: SortedMap<K, V>, key: K): Option.Option<V>; }
```

#### `SortedMap.getOrder`

**Replacement:** `none`

HashMap does not store an Order; retain and pass the key Order explicitly.

**Before**

```ts
getOrder: <K, V>(self: SortedMap<K, V>) => Order<K>
```

#### `SortedMap.headOption`

**Replacement:** `HashMap.entries + Array.sortWith + Array.head`

Sort entries by key with the retained Order, then take the optional first entry.

**Before**

```ts
headOption: <K, V>(self: SortedMap<K, V>) => Option.Option<[K, V]>
```

#### `SortedMap.isEmpty`

**Replacement:** `HashMap.isEmpty`

Direct emptiness check on the replacement immutable map.

**Before**

```ts
isEmpty: <K, V>(self: SortedMap<K, V>) => boolean
```

#### `SortedMap.isNonEmpty`

**Replacement:** `HashMap.isEmpty`

Use !HashMap.isEmpty(self); no dedicated HashMap.isNonEmpty helper exists.

**Before**

```ts
isNonEmpty: <K, V>(self: SortedMap<K, V>) => boolean
```

#### `SortedMap.isSortedMap`

**Replacement:** `HashMap.isHashMap`

Use the replacement model guard; it does not prove that observations were sorted.

**Before**

```ts
isSortedMap: { <K, V>(u: Iterable<readonly [K, V]>): u is SortedMap<K, V>; (u: unknown): u is SortedMap<unknown, unknown>; }
```

#### `SortedMap.keys`

**Replacement:** `HashMap.entries + Array.sortWith + Array.map`

Sort entries by key, map to keys, and iterate the resulting array.

**Before**

```ts
keys: <K, V>(self: SortedMap<K, V>) => IterableIterator<K>
```

#### `SortedMap.lastOption`

**Replacement:** `HashMap.entries + Array.sortWith + Array.last`

Sort entries by key with the retained Order, then take the optional last entry.

**Before**

```ts
lastOption: <K, V>(self: SortedMap<K, V>) => Option.Option<[K, V]>
```

#### `SortedMap.make`

**Replacement:** `HashMap.make`

Remove the outer order-curried constructor and pass entries directly to HashMap.make.

**Before**

```ts
make: <K>(ord: Order<K>) => <Entries extends ReadonlyArray<readonly [K, any]>>(...entries: Entries) => SortedMap<K, Entries[number] extends (readonly [any, infer V]) ? V : never>
```

#### `SortedMap.map`

**Replacement:** `HashMap.map`

The value-and-key callback remains, but result iteration is unordered until explicitly sorted.

**Before**

```ts
map: { <A, K, B>(f: (a: A, k: K) => B): (self: SortedMap<K, A>) => SortedMap<K, B>; <K, A, B>(self: SortedMap<K, A>, f: (a: A, k: K) => B): SortedMap<K, B>; }
```

#### `SortedMap.partition`

**Replacement:** `HashMap.filter`

Build [excluded, satisfying] with complementary HashMap.filter calls; adapt the callback to the old key predicate.

**Before**

```ts
partition: { <K, V>(predicate: (a: Types.NoInfer<K>) => boolean): (self: SortedMap<K, V>) => [excluded: SortedMap<K, V>, satisfying: SortedMap<K, V>]; <K, V>(self: SortedMap<K, V>, predicate: (a: K) => boolean): [excluded: SortedMap<K, V>, satisfying: SortedMap<K, V>]; }
```

#### `SortedMap.remove`

**Replacement:** `HashMap.remove`

Direct persistent removal; explicitly sort only when observing entries.

**Before**

```ts
remove: { <K>(key: K): <V>(self: SortedMap<K, V>) => SortedMap<K, V>; <K, V>(self: SortedMap<K, V>, key: K): SortedMap<K, V>; }
```

#### `SortedMap.set`

**Replacement:** `HashMap.set`

Direct persistent insert or update; explicitly sort only when observing entries.

**Before**

```ts
set: { <K, V>(key: K, value: V): (self: SortedMap<K, V>) => SortedMap<K, V>; <K, V>(self: SortedMap<K, V>, key: K, value: V): SortedMap<K, V>; }
```

#### `SortedMap.size`

**Replacement:** `HashMap.size`

Direct size query on the replacement immutable map.

**Before**

```ts
size: <K, V>(self: SortedMap<K, V>) => number
```

#### `SortedMap.values`

**Replacement:** `HashMap.entries + Array.sortWith + Array.map`

Sort entries by key, map to values, and iterate the resulting array.

**Before**

```ts
values: <K, V>(self: SortedMap<K, V>) => IterableIterator<V>
```

### `effect/SortedSet`

#### `SortedSet.SortedSet`

**Replacement:** `HashSet.HashSet`

Use HashSet as the immutable core model and retain Order externally; ordered iteration requires sorting on observation.

**Before**

```ts
export interface SortedSet<in out A> extends Iterable<A>, Equal.Equal, Pipeable, Inspectable { readonly [TypeId]: { readonly _A: Invariant<A>; }; }
```

#### `SortedSet.TypeId`

**Replacement:** `none`

The SortedSet brand was removed and HashSet.TypeId is private; use HashSet.isHashSet when a guard is needed.

**Before**

```ts
export type TypeId = typeof TypeId;
```

#### `SortedSet.add`

**Replacement:** `HashSet.add`

Direct persistent add on the replacement set; sort only when traversing.

**Before**

```ts
add: { <A>(value: A): (self: SortedSet<A>) => SortedSet<A>; <A>(self: SortedSet<A>, value: A): SortedSet<A>; }
```

#### `SortedSet.difference`

**Replacement:** `HashSet.difference + HashSet.fromIterable`

Convert the old general iterable argument to HashSet before taking the difference.

**Before**

```ts
difference: { <A, B extends A>(that: Iterable<B>): (self: SortedSet<A>) => SortedSet<A>; <A, B extends A>(self: SortedSet<A>, that: Iterable<B>): SortedSet<A>; }
```

#### `SortedSet.empty`

**Replacement:** `HashSet.empty`

SortedSet was removed; use an immutable HashSet and retain the element Order separately.

**Before**

```ts
empty: <A>(O: Order<A>) => SortedSet<A>
```

#### `SortedSet.filter`

**Replacement:** `HashSet.filter`

Direct persistent filtering on the replacement set; traversal is unordered until explicitly sorted.

**Before**

```ts
filter: { <A, B extends A>(predicate: Predicate<B>): (self: SortedSet<A>) => SortedSet<A>; <A>(self: SortedSet<A>, predicate: Predicate<A>): SortedSet<A>; }
```

#### `SortedSet.fromIterable`

**Replacement:** `HashSet.fromIterable`

Use HashSet.fromIterable and retain the element Order separately.

**Before**

```ts
fromIterable: { <B>(ord: Order<B>): <A extends B>(iterable: Iterable<A>) => SortedSet<A>; <A extends B, B>(iterable: Iterable<A>, ord: Order<B>): SortedSet<A>; }
```

#### `SortedSet.getEquivalence`

**Replacement:** `Equal.asEquivalence`

HashSet implements Effect equality by set content; use Equal.asEquivalence<HashSet.HashSet<A>>().

**Before**

```ts
getEquivalence: <A>() => Equivalence.Equivalence<SortedSet<A>>
```

#### `SortedSet.intersection`

**Replacement:** `HashSet.intersection + HashSet.fromIterable`

Convert the old general iterable argument to HashSet before taking the intersection.

**Before**

```ts
intersection: { <A>(that: Iterable<A>): (self: SortedSet<A>) => SortedSet<A>; <A>(self: SortedSet<A>, that: Iterable<A>): SortedSet<A>; }
```

#### `SortedSet.isSortedSet`

**Replacement:** `HashSet.isHashSet`

Use the replacement model guard; it does not prove that observations were sorted.

**Before**

```ts
isSortedSet: { <A>(u: Iterable<A>): u is SortedSet<A>; (u: unknown): u is SortedSet<unknown>; }
```

#### `SortedSet.make`

**Replacement:** `HashSet.make`

Remove the outer order-curried constructor and pass values directly to HashSet.make.

**Before**

```ts
make: <K>(ord: Order<K>) => <Entries extends ReadonlyArray<K>>(...entries: Entries) => SortedSet<Entries[number]>
```

#### `SortedSet.map`

**Replacement:** `HashSet.map`

Remove the output Order argument; retain it externally and sort only when traversing.

**Before**

```ts
map: { <B, A>(O: Order<B>, f: (a: A) => B): (self: SortedSet<A>) => SortedSet<B>; <B, A>(self: SortedSet<A>, O: Order<B>, f: (a: A) => B): SortedSet<B>; }
```

#### `SortedSet.partition`

**Replacement:** `HashSet.filter`

Build [excluded, satisfying] with complementary HashSet.filter calls.

**Before**

```ts
partition: { <A>(predicate: (a: NoInfer<A>) => boolean): (self: SortedSet<A>) => [excluded: SortedSet<A>, satisfying: SortedSet<A>]; <A>(self: SortedSet<A>, predicate: (a: A) => boolean): [excluded: SortedSet<A>, satisfying: SortedSet<A>]; }
```

#### `SortedSet.remove`

**Replacement:** `HashSet.remove`

Direct persistent removal on the replacement set.

**Before**

```ts
remove: { <A>(value: A): (self: SortedSet<A>) => SortedSet<A>; <A>(self: SortedSet<A>, value: A): SortedSet<A>; }
```

#### `SortedSet.size`

**Replacement:** `HashSet.size`

Direct size query on the replacement immutable set.

**Before**

```ts
size: <A>(self: SortedSet<A>) => number
```

#### `SortedSet.union`

**Replacement:** `HashSet.union + HashSet.fromIterable`

Convert the old general iterable argument to HashSet before taking the union.

**Before**

```ts
union: { <A>(that: Iterable<A>): (self: SortedSet<A>) => SortedSet<A>; <A>(self: SortedSet<A>, that: Iterable<A>): SortedSet<A>; }
```

#### `SortedSet.values`

**Replacement:** `Array.sort`

Sort the replacement HashSet with the retained Order and iterate the resulting array.

**Before**

```ts
values: <A>(self: SortedSet<A>) => IterableIterator<A>
```

### `effect/Stream`

#### `Stream.Stream`

**Replacement:** `Stream`

The Stream<A, E, R> interface is unchanged in shape and keeps the effect/Stream import path; the type-id key is now the string literal "~effect/Stream" instead of a unique symbol.

**Before**

```ts
export declare namespace Stream { interface Variance<out A, out E, out R> { readonly [StreamTypeId]: VarianceStruct<A, E, R>; } interface VarianceStruct<out A, out E, out R> { readonly _A: Covariant<A>; readonly _E: Covariant<E>; readonly _R: Covariant<R>; } type Success<T extends Stream<any, any, any>> = [T] extends [Stream<infer _A, infer _E, infer _R>] ? _A : never; type Error<T extends Stream<any, any, any>> = [T] extends [Stream<infer _A, infer _E, infer _R>] ? _E : never; type Context<T extends Stream<any, any, any>> = [T] extends [Stream<infer _A, infer _E, infer _R>] ? _R : never; type DynamicTuple<T, N extends number> = N extends N ? number extends N ? Array<T> : DynamicTupleOf<T, N, []> : never; type DynamicTupleOf<T, N extends number, R extends Array<unknown>> = R["length"] extends N ? R : DynamicTupleOf<T, N, [T, ...R]>; }
```

**After**

```ts
isStream: (u: unknown) => u is Stream<unknown, unknown, unknown>
```

#### `Stream.Stream.Context`

**Replacement:** `Stream.Services`

Type-level extractor of the R parameter renamed from Stream.Context<T> to Stream.Services<T>; identical conditional-infer semantics.

**Before**

```ts
type Context<T extends Stream<any, any, any>> = [T] extends [Stream<infer _A, infer _E, infer _R>] ? _R : never;
```

#### `Stream.Stream.DynamicTuple`

**Replacement:** `Types.TupleOf`

Already deprecated in v3 in favor of Types.TupleOf; removed in v4. Use Types.TupleOf<N, T> (v4 Stream.broadcastN uses it for its return type).

**Before**

```ts
type DynamicTuple<T, N extends number> = N extends N ? number extends N ? Array<T> : DynamicTupleOf<T, N, []> : never;
```

- `Stream.Stream.DynamicTupleOf` -> `Types.TupleOf`: Recursive tuple-builder helper removed with Stream.DynamicTuple; Types.TupleOf<N, T> is the v4 equivalent.

#### `Stream.StreamTypeId`

**Replacement:** `Stream.TypeId`

Renamed StreamTypeId -> TypeId and changed from a unique symbol to the string literal "~effect/Stream" (both the const and the type).

**Before**

```ts
export type StreamTypeId = typeof StreamTypeId;
```

#### `Stream.StreamUnify`

**Replacement:** `Stream.StreamUnify`

Still exported under the same name in v4 (extends Effect.EffectUnify); no change needed besides any Chunk-related element types.

**Before**

```ts
export interface StreamUnify<A extends { [Unify.typeSymbol]?: any; }> extends Effect.EffectUnify<A> { Stream?: () => A[Unify.typeSymbol] extends Stream<infer A0, infer E0, infer R0> | infer _ ? Stream<A0, E0, R0> : never; }
```

**After**

```ts
export interface StreamUnify<A extends { [Unify.typeSymbol]?: any; }> extends Effect.EffectUnify<A> { Stream?: () => A[Unify.typeSymbol] extends Stream<infer A0, infer E0, infer R0> | infer _ ? Stream<A0, E0, R0> : never; }
```

#### `Stream.StreamUnifyIgnore`

**Replacement:** `Stream.StreamUnifyIgnore`

Still exported under the same name in v4 (extends Effect.EffectUnifyIgnore with Effect ignored); unchanged.

**Before**

```ts
export interface StreamUnifyIgnore extends Effect.EffectUnifyIgnore { Effect?: true; }
```

**After**

```ts
export interface StreamUnifyIgnore { Effect?: true; }
```

#### `Stream.accumulateChunks`

**Replacement:** `none`

v3 accumulateChunks only rewrote the internal chunk layout (each chunk cumulatively contained all prior elements) without changing the emitted element sequence; v4 has no chunk-layout twin. Stream.accumulate emits the cumulative NonEmptyArray values, and Stream.rechunk controls chunk sizing.

**Before**

```ts
accumulateChunks: <A, E, R>(self: Stream<A, E, R>) => Stream<A, E, R>
```

#### `Stream.acquireRelease`

**Replacement:** `Stream.scoped(Stream.fromEffect(Effect.acquireRelease(acquire, release)))`

Dedicated constructor removed; compose Effect.acquireRelease (same (resource, exit) release signature) with Stream.fromEffect, then Stream.scoped to tie the finalizer to the stream's lifetime.

**Before**

```ts
acquireRelease: <A, E, R, R2, X>(acquire: Effect.Effect<A, E, R>, release: (resource: A, exit: Exit.Exit<unknown, unknown>) => Effect.Effect<X, never, R2>) => Stream<A, E, R | R2>
```

#### `Stream.aggregateWithinEither`

**Replacement:** `Stream.aggregateWithin`

Either-emitting variant removed; v4 aggregateWithin(sink, schedule) emits only the sink outputs B (schedule outputs are no longer surfaced as Either.right).

**Before**

```ts
aggregateWithinEither: { <B, A, A2, E2, R2, C, R3>(sink: Sink.Sink<B, A | A2, A2, E2, R2>, schedule: Schedule.Schedule<C, Option.Option<B>, R3>): <E, R>(self: Stream<A, E, R>) => Stream<Either.Either<B, C>, E2 | E, R2 | R3 | R>; <A, E, R, B, A2, E2, R2, C, R3>(self: Stream<A, E, R>, sink: Sink.Sink<B, A | A2, A2, E2, R2>, schedule: Schedule.Schedule<C, Option.Option<B>, R3>): Stream<Either.Either<B, C>, E | E2, R | R2 | R3>; }
```

#### `Stream.as`

**Replacement:** `Stream.map(() => value)`

Stream.as was removed; replace each element with a constant via Stream.map.

**Before**

```ts
as: { <B>(value: B): <A, E, R>(self: Stream<A, E, R>) => Stream<B, E, R>; <A, E, R, B>(self: Stream<A, E, R>, value: B): Stream<B, E, R>; }
```

#### `Stream.async`

**Replacement:** `Stream.callback`

Stream.callback((queue) => Effect | void, { bufferSize?, strategy? }) replaces the Emit-based async; push with Queue.offer/offerAll, end with Queue.end, fail with Queue.fail.

**Before**

```ts
_async: <A, E = never, R = never>(register: (emit: Emit.Emit<R, E, A, void>) => Effect.Effect<void, never, R> | void, bufferSize?: number | "unbounded" | { readonly bufferSize?: number | undefined; readonly strategy?: "dropping" | "sliding" | "suspend" | undefined; } | undefined) => Stream<A, E, R>
```

#### `Stream.asyncEffect`

**Replacement:** `Stream.callback`

The register function of Stream.callback may return an Effect (run before the stream starts pulling), covering asyncEffect; signal end/failure through the provided Queue.

**Before**

```ts
asyncEffect: <A, E = never, R = never>(register: (emit: Emit.Emit<R, E, A, void>) => Effect.Effect<unknown, E, R>, bufferSize?: number | "unbounded" | { readonly bufferSize?: number | undefined; readonly strategy?: "dropping" | "sliding" | "suspend" | undefined; } | undefined) => Stream<A, E, R>
```

#### `Stream.asyncPush`

**Replacement:** `Stream.callback`

Stream.callback's register effect can use Scope for acquire/release of the external subscription, replacing asyncPush; the Emit ops helpers become plain Queue operations.

**Before**

```ts
asyncPush: <A, E = never, R = never>(register: (emit: Emit.EmitOpsPush<E, A>) => Effect.Effect<unknown, E, R | Scope.Scope>, options?: { readonly bufferSize: "unbounded"; } | { readonly bufferSize?: number | undefined; readonly strategy?: "dropping" | "sliding" | undefined; } | undefined) => Stream<A, E, Exclude<R, Scope.Scope>>
```

#### `Stream.asyncScoped`

**Replacement:** `Stream.callback`

Stream.callback's register effect may use Scope (Scope is excluded from the resulting R), replacing asyncScoped; the Option<E> end signal becomes Queue.end.

**Before**

```ts
asyncScoped: <A, E = never, R = never>(register: (emit: Emit.Emit<R, E, A, void>) => Effect.Effect<unknown, E, R | Scope.Scope>, bufferSize?: number | "unbounded" | { readonly bufferSize?: number | undefined; readonly strategy?: "dropping" | "sliding" | "suspend" | undefined; } | undefined) => Stream<A, E, Exclude<R, Scope.Scope>>
```

#### `Stream.branchAfter`

**Replacement:** `Stream.peel`

Removed; the closest v4 primitive is Stream.peel(self, Sink.take(n)), a scoped Effect yielding [firstN, restStream] from which you build the continuation stream and re-wrap with Stream.unwrap.

**Before**

```ts
branchAfter: { <A, A2, E2, R2>(n: number, f: (input: Chunk.Chunk<A>) => Stream<A2, E2, R2>): <E, R>(self: Stream<A, E, R>) => Stream<A2, E2 | E, R2 | R>; <A, E, R, A2, E2, R2>(self: Stream<A, E, R>, n: number, f: (input: Chunk.Chunk<A>) => Stream<A2, E2, R2>): Stream<A2, E | E2, R | R2>; }
```

**Example**

```ts
Stream.unwrap(Effect.map(Stream.peel(self, Sink.take(n)), ([head, rest]) => f(head)(rest)))
```

- `Stream.broadcastDynamic` -> `Stream.broadcast`: v4 Stream.broadcast({ capacity, strategy?, replay? }) is the dynamic-subscriber fan-out returning Effect<Stream<A, E>, never, Scope | R> (v3 fixed-arity broadcast(n) became Stream.broadcastN); Stream.share adds refcounted/idleTimeToLive semantics.

#### `Stream.broadcastedQueues`

**Replacement:** `none`

Queue-of-Take fan-out surface removed. Use Stream.broadcastN({ n, capacity }) for a fixed tuple of mirror streams, or Stream.toPubSubTake to obtain a PubSub of Take values and subscribe consumers to it.

**Before**

```ts
broadcastedQueues: { <N extends number>(n: N, maximumLag: number | { readonly capacity: "unbounded"; readonly replay?: number | undefined; } | { readonly capacity: number; readonly strategy?: "sliding" | "dropping" | "suspend" | undefined; readonly replay?: number | undefined; }): <A, E, R>(self: Stream<A, E, R>) => Effect.Effect<TupleOf<N, Queue.Dequeue<Take.Take<A, E>>>, never, Scope.Scope | R>; <A, E, R, N extends number>(self: Stream<A, E, R>, n: N, maximumLag: number | { readonly capacity: "unbounded"; readonly replay?: number | undefined; } | { readonly capacity: number; readonly strategy?: "sliding" | "dropping" | "suspend" | undefined; readonly replay?: number | undefined; }): Effect.Effect<TupleOf<N, Queue.Dequeue<Take.Take<A, E>>>, never, Scope.Scope | R>; }
```

#### `Stream.broadcastedQueuesDynamic`

**Replacement:** `none`

Removed with broadcastedQueues. Use Stream.broadcast (dynamic mirror streams) or Stream.toPubSubTake + PubSub subscriptions when raw Take-level consumers are needed.

**Before**

```ts
broadcastedQueuesDynamic: { (maximumLag: number | { readonly capacity: "unbounded"; readonly replay?: number | undefined; } | { readonly capacity: number; readonly strategy?: "sliding" | "dropping" | "suspend" | undefined; readonly replay?: number | undefined; }): <A, E, R>(self: Stream<A, E, R>) => Effect.Effect<Effect.Effect<Queue.Dequeue<Take.Take<A, E>>, never, Scope.Scope>, never, Scope.Scope | R>; <A, E, R>(self: Stream<A, E, R>, maximumLag: number | { readonly capacity: "unbounded"; readonly replay?: number | undefined; } | { readonly capacity: number; readonly strategy?: "sliding" | "dropping" | "suspend" | undefined; readonly replay?: number | undefined; }): Effect.Effect<Effect.Effect<Queue.Dequeue<Take.Take<A, E>>, never, Scope.Scope>, never, Scope.Scope | R>; }
```

#### `Stream.bufferChunks`

**Replacement:** `Stream.bufferArray`

Chunk->Array rename; buffers whole arrays (chunks) up to capacity with the same strategy options.

**Before**

```ts
bufferChunks: { (options: { readonly capacity: number; readonly strategy?: "dropping" | "sliding" | "suspend" | undefined; }): <A, E, R>(self: Stream<A, E, R>) => Stream<A, E, R>; <A, E, R>(self: Stream<A, E, R>, options: { readonly capacity: number; readonly strategy?: "dropping" | "sliding" | "suspend" | undefined; }): Stream<A, E, R>; }
```

- `Stream.catchAll` -> `Stream.catch`: Renamed to Stream.catch (exported keyword-style); same (error) => Stream handler for all typed failures.

- `Stream.catchAllCause` -> `Stream.catchCause`: Renamed; handler receives the full Cause<E> and returns a recovery stream, identical semantics.

#### `Stream.catchSome`

**Replacement:** `Stream.catchFilter`

Option-returning partial handler replaced by the Filter API: Stream.catchFilter(filter, f, orElse?) recovers matched errors, unmatched failures pass through (Stream.catchIf for refinement/predicate matching).

**Before**

```ts
catchSome: { <E, A2, E2, R2>(pf: (error: E) => Option.Option<Stream<A2, E2, R2>>): <A, R>(self: Stream<A, E, R>) => Stream<A2 | A, E | E2, R2 | R>; <A, E, R, A2, E2, R2>(self: Stream<A, E, R>, pf: (error: E) => Option.Option<Stream<A2, E2, R2>>): Stream<A | A2, E | E2, R | R2>; }
```

#### `Stream.catchSomeCause`

**Replacement:** `Stream.catchCauseFilter`

Option-returning cause handler replaced by Stream.catchCauseFilter(filter, f, orElse?) using a Filter on the Cause (Stream.catchCauseIf for refinements).

**Before**

```ts
catchSomeCause: { <E, A2, E2, R2>(pf: (cause: Cause.Cause<E>) => Option.Option<Stream<A2, E2, R2>>): <A, R>(self: Stream<A, E, R>) => Stream<A2 | A, E | E2, R2 | R>; <A, E, R, A2, E2, R2>(self: Stream<A, E, R>, pf: (cause: Cause.Cause<E>) => Option.Option<Stream<A2, E2, R2>>): Stream<A | A2, E | E2, R | R2>; }
```

#### `Stream.chunksWith`

**Replacement:** `Stream.flattenArray(f(Stream.chunks(self)))`

No dedicated combinator; expose chunk structure with Stream.chunks (Stream<NonEmptyReadonlyArray<A>>), transform, then re-flatten with Stream.flattenArray.

**Before**

```ts
chunksWith: { <A, E, R, A2, E2, R2>(f: (stream: Stream<Chunk.Chunk<A>, E, R>) => Stream<Chunk.Chunk<A2>, E2, R2>): (self: Stream<A, E, R>) => Stream<A2, E | E2, R | R2>; <A, E, R, A2, E2, R2>(self: Stream<A, E, R>, f: (stream: Stream<Chunk.Chunk<A>, E, R>) => Stream<Chunk.Chunk<A2>, E2, R2>): Stream<A2, E | E2, R | R2>; }
```

#### `Stream.combineChunks`

**Replacement:** `Stream.combineArray`

Chunk->Array rename of the pull-level combining primitive; pulls now yield NonEmptyReadonlyArray values and halt via Cause.Done-failing Pull effects instead of Option-typed errors.

**Before**

```ts
combineChunks: { <A2, E2, R2, S, R3, E, A, R4, R5, A3>(that: Stream<A2, E2, R2>, s: S, f: (s: S, pullLeft: Effect.Effect<Chunk.Chunk<A>, Option.Option<E>, R3>, pullRight: Effect.Effect<Chunk.Chunk<A2>, Option.Option<E2>, R4>) => Effect.Effect<Exit.Exit<readonly [Chunk.Chunk<A3>, S], Option.Option<E2 | E>>, never, R5>): <R>(self: Stream<A, E, R>) => Stream<A3, E2 | E, R2 | R3 | R4 | R5 | R>; <R, A2, E2, R2, S, R3, E, A, R4, R5, A3>(self: Stream<A, E, R>, that: Stream<A2, E2, R2>, s: S, f: (s: S, pullLeft: Effect.Effect<Chunk.Chunk<A>, Option.Option<E>, R3>, pullRight: Effect.Effect<Chunk.Chunk<A2>, Option.Option<E2>, R4>) => Effect.Effect<Exit.Exit<readonly [Chunk.Chunk<A3>, S], Option.Option<E2 | E>>, never, R5>): Stream<A3, E2 | E, R | R2 | R3 | R4 | R5>; }
```

#### `Stream.concatAll`

**Replacement:** `Stream.flatten`

Chunk-of-streams constructor removed; sequential concatenation of many streams is Stream.flatten(Stream.fromIterable(streams)) (default concurrency 1 preserves order).

**Before**

```ts
concatAll: <A, E, R>(streams: Chunk.Chunk<Stream<A, E, R>>) => Stream<A, E, R>
```

#### `Stream.context`

**Replacement:** `Stream.fromEffect(Effect.context<R>())`

Dedicated accessor removed; lift Effect.context<R>() into a single-element stream.

**Before**

```ts
context: <R>() => Stream<Context.Context<R>, never, R>
```

#### `Stream.contextWith`

**Replacement:** `Stream.fromEffect(Effect.contextWith(f))`

Dedicated accessor removed; Effect.contextWith still exists in v4, lift it with Stream.fromEffect.

**Before**

```ts
contextWith: <R, A>(f: (env: Context.Context<R>) => A) => Stream<A, never, R>
```

#### `Stream.contextWithEffect`

**Replacement:** `Stream.fromEffect(Effect.flatMap(Effect.context<R0>(), f))`

Removed; read the Context with Effect.context, feed it to the effectful function, and lift the result with Stream.fromEffect.

**Before**

```ts
contextWithEffect: <R0, A, E, R>(f: (env: Context.Context<R0>) => Effect.Effect<A, E, R>) => Stream<A, E, R0 | R>
```

#### `Stream.contextWithStream`

**Replacement:** `Stream.unwrap(Effect.contextWith(f))`

Removed; build the dependent stream inside Effect.contextWith and flatten with Stream.unwrap.

**Before**

```ts
contextWithStream: <R0, A, E, R>(f: (env: Context.Context<R0>) => Stream<A, E, R>) => Stream<A, E, R0 | R>
```

#### `Stream.crossLeft`

**Replacement:** `Stream.crossWith(that, (a, _) => a)`

Removed; cartesian product keeping only left elements is expressed with Stream.crossWith and a left-projecting combiner.

**Before**

```ts
crossLeft: { <AR, ER, RR>(right: Stream<AR, ER, RR>): <AL, EL, RL>(left: Stream<AL, EL, RL>) => Stream<AL, EL | ER, RL | RR>; <AL, EL, RL, AR, ER, RR>(left: Stream<AL, EL, RL>, right: Stream<AR, ER, RR>): Stream<AL, EL | ER, RL | RR>; }
```

#### `Stream.crossRight`

**Replacement:** `Stream.crossWith(that, (_, b) => b)`

Removed; cartesian product keeping only right elements is Stream.crossWith with a right-projecting combiner (equivalently Stream.flatMap(self, () => that)).

**Before**

```ts
crossRight: { <AR, ER, RR>(right: Stream<AR, ER, RR>): <AL, EL, RL>(left: Stream<AL, EL, RL>) => Stream<AR, EL | ER, RL | RR>; <AL, EL, RL, AR, ER, RR>(left: Stream<AL, EL, RL>, right: Stream<AR, ER, RR>): Stream<AR, EL | ER, RL | RR>; }
```

#### `Stream.dieMessage`

**Replacement:** `Stream.die(new Error(message))`

Removed along with RuntimeException; die with an explicit defect value via Stream.die.

**Before**

```ts
dieMessage: (message: string) => Stream<never>
```

#### `Stream.dieSync`

**Replacement:** `Stream.failCauseSync(() => Cause.die(evaluate()))`

Removed; lazily construct the defect cause with Cause.die inside Stream.failCauseSync.

**Before**

